sources.note: Union of every page in the unfiltered directory and all nine status filters. Includes programs and studies. URLs are deduplicated; publication ordering can vary.

projects.name: 2690 Geary Blvd
projects.description: Interior remodel of existing space to become new Public Storage regional office space

projects.name: 700 INDIANA ST
projects.description: The proposal is request for a Large Project Authorization, pursuant to Planning Code Section 329 and 838 to allow a project greater than 25,000 square feet of floor area with exceptions to allow for reduced rear yard and modification to horizontal mass reduction requirement for large lots (270.1). The Project includes demolition of an existing one-story 15,000 sq. ft. warehouse building for construction of a three-story Non-Life Science laboratory building approximately 70,650 sq. ft. in size, containing 51 off-street parking spaces and 2 car-share spaces below grade, one off-street loading space, 15 bicycle parking spaces consisting of 6 Class One bicycle spaces, 5 Class One bicycle fleet spaces, 4 Class Two bicycle spaces; 4 showers, private bike repair station, 24 lockers, and approximately 8,000 sq. ft. of non-residential open space at rooftop level of the subject property within the UMU (Urban Mixed Use) Zoning District and 58-X Height and Bulk District. Pursuant to Planning Code Section 295, the Commission must adopt findings that the additional shadow cast by the Project on Esprit Park would not be adverse to the use of this park.

projects.name: 1229 Underwood Avenue
projects.description: Demolition of an unwarranted building per 2020-00699ENF

projects.name: 2270 Jerrold Avenue
projects.description: Demolition of an existing office building that was recently damaged due to a fire caused by a homeless encampment on the adjacent public sidewalk.

projects.name: 75 WATERLOO ST
projects.description: The project proposes installation of (117) new Supercharger posts, (1) new switchgear, (15) supercharging cabinets, (28) parking lot lights, (23) trash receptacles, Trash enclosure with (2) trash bins, (88) drilled bollards, (81) bolt down bollards, (30) offset bollards, (15) folding PSU's (2) new restrooms and vending amenity. Includes removal of (1) existing 6739 sq. ft. building, removal of existing 378 sq ft roof canopy.

projects.name: 12 MINT PLZ
projects.description: To Comply with Planning Code Enforcement Case No. 2023-009082ENF. The proposed project is to legalize the change of use from a credit union to group housing. The project complies with group housing requirements as is, except for the need to add a full stove to comply with the Planning Code. There are 15 bedroom equivalent group housing units and 1 kitchen. Also, the amount of common space exceeds the 0.5 feet of common space for every 1 foot of private space ratio required. At least 15% of that common space is in the communal kitchen area, as required. Aside from the addition of a stove to the kitchen, we are proposing no changes to the as-built condition. We just want to change the use to group housing, which is an explicitly allowed use in the C3-G zone. 100 percent of these group housing units will be affordable to anyone earning 50 percent of the area median income. We currently charge $700 per month, inclusive of utilities and internet, which is affordable even for those who qualify as extremely low income.

projects.name: 5500-5504 MISSION STREET
projects.description: The proposal is to merge four parcels into one 8,705-square-foot lot, demolish the existing auto repiar building, and construct a new four-story, residential care building (RCFE) for the elderly with the main entrance on Mission Street. The building will provide 30 rooms and 49 RCFE beds for ambulatory and non-ambulatory patients. A white loading zone will be created on Mission Street and access to one vehicle and four Class I bicycle spaces will be on Foote Avenue. The sidewalk will also contain six Class II bicycle spaces and 10 new street trees. Open space will be located on a second floor, rear deck.

projects.name: 1401 Illinois Street, 1298 Michigan Street, and 1499 Illinois Street
projects.address: 1401 Illinois Street, 1298 Michigan Street, and 1499 Illinois Street
projects.description: Demolish 8 existing warehouse buildings consisting of 34,940 square feet. Construction of paved surface lots within the footprint of the demolished buildings. Establish a Storage Yard use. Grading and installation of site stormwater drainage will be performed as needed. No modification of the existing surface lots. New fencing with screening will be installed to match existing and manual gates will be installed at curb cuts. No new curb cuts are proposed. The 23 existing parking spaces would be retained, and no new parking spaces are proposed.

projects.name: 2007 FRANKLIN ST
projects.description: SF Heritage proposes to formalize General Entertainment, Nighttime Entertainment, and Bar uses and Outdoor Activity Area in the front and rear gardens of the Property (the “Project”). The Project maintains the existing uses of the Property, including as a residence, museum, office, and events space. The Project seeks Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code Sections 186.3, 209.1, 303, and 710 for General Entertainment, Nighttime Entertainment, and Bar uses and Outdoor Activity Area. The Project seeks to formalize the Outdoor Activity Area in the front and rear gardens of the Property pursuant to Planning Code Sections 145.2, 186.3, 209.1, 303, and 710. The Project will generate increased revenue needed to maintain this landmark building. Allowing these uses will enhance the feasibility of preserving the landmark building for another 130 years. No alteration or construction is proposed by the Project.

projects.name: 2700 45TH AVE
projects.description: Conditional Use Authorization application request pursuant to Planning Code Section 303 for the development of large lot within the NC-2 Zoning District (Section 121.1), a non-residential use exceeding 4,000 square feet (Section 121.2), and establishment of an Institutional Use at the second and above floors (Section 711). The proposes project includes ground floor indoor pool and aquatic center, mezzanine storage, and 52 vehicular parking spaces. The first floor lobby includes digital gallery and emerald pub, 2FL mezzanine, banquet and theater seating, 3FL Dowling library and Irish museum, 4FL, Administrative offices and classrooms, 5th FL gym and 6th FL restuarant and bar, roof deck and garden.

projects.name: 1035 HOWARD STREET
projects.description: The project requests a Major Permit to Alter from the Historic Preservation Commission to convert 17,549 gross square feet (gsf) of existing vacant Laboratory and Office use to Self-Storage and convert approximately 43,996 gsf of existing vacant Production, Distribution, and Repair (PDR) use to Commercial Storage (a PDR use). Additionally, a one-story mechanical room at the rear of the building would be demolished and existing skylights would be infilled, with their curbs preserved for future restoration. The Howard Street main entry would be restored, and original industrial windows on the primary façade (Howard Street) would be repaired and rehabilitated with glazing salvaged from other windows at the property. Windows on the Russ Street façade would be replaced with new, single-pane transparent laminated glass metal-sash windows to match the existing in terms of panel size and configuration. The project also includes improvements to an existing surface area at the rear on the Russ Street frontage to allow accessory parking and loading. No expansion to the existing building envelope is proposed.

projects.name: 530 SANSOME ST
projects.description: The Project proposes construction of two new buildings: (1) a new 41-story mixed use building, approximately 544-foot tall (approximately 574-feet including mechanical penthouses and screening) containing approximately 375,000 square feet of Office use, 210,000 square feet of Hotel use, and 7,500 square feet of lower-level Retail Restaurant & Bar use, all located at 530 Sansome St and adjacent parcels; and (2) a new Fire Station 13 located at 447 Battery Street site (corner of Battery and Merchant streets) (the “Project”). The Project would require the demolition of the existing improvements on the project site.

projects.name: 400 BAY STREET
projects.description: The project proposes to modify the new mixed-use (Hotel and Retail) building, approved by the Planning Commission on August 6, 2015 (Motion No. 19427), with a 10-foot Horizontal Addition.

projects.name: Canabis 311 - 100 BROADWAY
projects.description: Change of use from office to cannabis retail. Other office spaces remain.

projects.name: 312 COLUMBUS AVE
projects.description: The project proposes the ground floor storefront merger of 310 Columbus Avenue and 312 Columbus Avenue, formerly Little Darings, to expand the lobby area of the Europa Hotel. The remodel will include a new lobby/lounge, entry vestibule, toilets, hotel offices, stall-only laundry and utilities, and hotel storage.

projects.name: 2190 OFARRELL ST
projects.description: Replacement Hospital Project consists of the demolition of three existing on-site structures, and proposes the construction of two new buildings (a replacement hospital building and parking garage). The proposed replacement hospital building will be 694,012 SF (Gross Floor Area, SF Planning Code Section 102) approximately 266’ in height with 14 floors. The proposed parking garage will be 534,274 SF (Gross Floor Area, SF Planning Code Section 102) approximately 100’ in height with 12 floors (7 levels above grade and 5 levels below grade) and will provide 1,003 parking spaces.

projects.name: 2331 31ST AVE
projects.description: The project proposes a ground floor change of use to convert the existing garage and workshop to a childcare (3-month to 5-year old). Center will provide care for 35 children. Add an outdoor staircase to the second floor. Master bedroom suite remodel w/layout change. Den and bedroom remodel w/layout change. Kitchen remodel w/layout change. Add deck.

projects.name: 2345 WAWONA ST
projects.description: The project proposes conversion of an existing garage and living area into a childcare center to accommodate children aged 3 months to 5 years, with a capacity for up to 22 kids. At the second floor, laundry facilities would be relocated to the bathroom, optimizing the space and functionality of the upper level.

projects.name: 40 12TH ST
projects.description: Project seeks to convert an existing Storage building into a new Bathhouse (an Adult Sex Venue). The building has approximately 7,650 sq.ft. on 2 stories and a mezzanine. The Bathhouse shall feature shower rooms, locker rooms, a steam room and multiple rooms for patrons to engage in sexual activities or watch other patrons engaging in sexual activities. The project would involve approximately 200 cubic yards of excavation (with a maximum depth of 6 feet).

projects.name: 50 Otis Street / 95 Brady Street
projects.description: Merging two tenant spaces for single occupant of two-story building. The occupant is a photo-booth company. The work includes modifications to building entrances on Otis and Brady Streets, to have out swinging doors. On First Floor: new showroom/sales space and stockroom, and new toilet rooms. On Second Floor: new offices and new mezzanine storage. Work includes new storefront, partitions, doors, glazing, lighting, electrical, plumbing and finishes, and a new VRC lift between the two floors.

projects.name: 43 Norfolk Street
projects.description: The Project proposes a change of use of a 1,741 square foot, two-story Industrial building to Cannabis Retail, with no on-site smoking or vaporizing of cannabis products.

projects.name: Outdoor dining patio · 2214 Mission
projects.description: The project proposes to convert the private parking lot to an outdoor dining area/patio.
projects.summary: A proposal to turn a private parking lot into an outdoor dining patio. The record does not identify the operator. This is not evidence of a new restaurant opening.

projects.name: 2325 03RD ST
projects.description: Change of use from manufacturing warehouse to new solid state hydrogen production facility (915 square feet).

projects.name: 1840 OAKDALE AVENUE
projects.description: The proposal is for a two-story commercial building on the subject lot.

projects.name: 2285 JERROLD AVE - Modified Project
projects.description: The Project requests a modification of the Conditional Use Authorization approved under Case No. 2018-013692CUA (Motion No.20883) pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 210.3 to establish an Internet Service Exchange. There are no proposed modifications to the PUD that were a part of the original approval but are included as a part of this modification review.

projects.name: 3501 CESAR CHAVEZ ST
projects.description: This project is part of Development Agreement 2012.0403W between the City and County of San Francisco and Sutter Health dba California Pacific Medical Center. The project received environmental clearance through an addendum to CPMC's Long Range Development Plan EIR 2005.0555E. The Mission Bernal Campus Medical Office Building (MOB) is an approximately 129,000 sq ft, five-story building, including health services/medical office space, retail and parking on four below ground levels including approximately 210 parking spaces, with vehicular access to the parking garage from Cesar Chavez and Valencia Streets. The pedestrian access points are from the lobby entrances on the lower plaza level, the upper plaza level, and the vehicular drop off is on the first floor inside the garage. Bicyle access is through a dedicated door off Valencia Street. The MOB will have a connection to the adjacent hospital via a corridor under the upper plaza which will be permitted separately through the Office of Statewide Health Planning and Development (OSHPD).

projects.name: 240 COTTER ST
projects.description: The project proposes a 1,094 sq. ft., two-story, horizontal addition and includes the following scopes: convert the existing garage at the ground level to a childcare center (approximately 1,185 square feet) for three-month to five-year old children with a maximum of 25 children and a remodel of the second floor living area with the addition of an outdoor staircase.

projects.name: 32 CLEMENT ST
projects.description: Proposed 11th location of a retail store named "Therapy Stores" in an existing first floor, tenant space. A Conditional Use authorization is sought pursuant to Planning Code Section 303.1 for a Formula Retail change of use from Medical Office to General Retail Sales and Service use. Modification of the existing exterior awning is also proposed.

projects.name: 401 South Van Ness
projects.description: The project proposes demolition of an existing fenced parking lot to build a new construction of an 11-story mixed-use building which includes a 3,271 SF of commercial tenant space on the ground level and group housing above grade with 182 bedroom suites and shared amenity spaces on every level.

projects.name: 2741 16th Street
projects.description: To erect 4 stories, type 1, parking/mech and pdr/lab

projects.name: Bookstore & restaurant · former Hibernia Bank
projects.description: The project proposes a change of use from Institutional (Other Institution, Large) to Retail (Limited-Restaurant and bookstore), including the addition of an Outdoor Eating and Drinking area located behind the building, pursuant to Planning Code Section 202.2 (Eating and Drinking Uses) and Section 202.2(a)(7) (Outdoor Activity Conditions of Approval).Exterior scope consists of the replacement of non-historic windows and doors with compatible new slim-profile metal windows and door and rehabilitation of exterior masonry and cast iron elements, restoration of an existing skylight and relocation of a roof hatch for rooftop access for maintenance purposes.
projects.summary: A proposed bookstore, restaurant and events space in the former Social Security office at 22nd and Valencia, with outdoor dining. No trading name or opening date verified.

projects.name: 1026 MISSION ST
projects.description: The proposed project (“Project”) would convert approximately 34,000 gross square feet within the existing, vacant commercial building from Retail (Fringe Financial Service) and Office use to Self-Storage use. The Project includes associated interior tenant improvements on the basement, first, mezzanine, and third floors of the subject property, with no exterior changes proposed.

projects.name: 555 MARKET STREET
projects.description: The project on floors one (ground floor) and two of an existing 22-story high-rise located at 555 Market Street include improvements to the existing lobby space and construction of tenant amenity spaces, conference rooms, and fitness areas. The scope also includes a change of use on level one for a new public-facing bar and restaurant along Market Street. The new bar space will include an outdoor terrace that wraps around the base of the tower podium, which will require the installation of a glass railing around the perimeter of the podium.

projects.name: 350 02ND ST
projects.description: The proposal consists of the construction of a new 130 foot tall, 14-story building with 297 guest rooms, 166,415 sf hotel; 2,975 sf of ground floor restaurant/bar and related back of house space; 2,350 sf of ground floor privately owned public open space; and 9,100 sf of off-street parking for 18 valet spaces. The building will feature a 7- story, 65 foot tall podium with a 14-story, 130 foot tall tower.

projects.name: 60 FEDERAL ST
projects.description: The project proposes converting the existing building from office (94,657 square feet) to self-storage (83,935 square feet). No expansion to the existing building envelope is proposed. Physical improvements would be limited to interior work necessary to accommodate self-storage and minor exterior modifications.

projects.name: 620 03RD ST
projects.description: The generally rectangular-shaped project site is located at 620 3rd Street midblock on 3rd Street between Brannan and Townsend streets. The project site consists of block/lot number 3787/005. The site is developed with a two-story, 41,680 square-foot warehouse building, which is a contributory structure to the Clyde and Crooks Warehouses Historic District, that is currently used as a data center. The project proposes a third-story vertical addition consisting of 16,296 square feet of office use and the conversion of the existing data center use to office use. In total, the project would contain 49,990 square feet of office space. The proposed project would also include 2,567 square feet of ground floor retail along the 3rd Street frontage, 10 class I and three class II bicycle spaces, bicycle showers and lockers, 943 square feet of private open space at the third floor, and a solar-ready and living roof area. Proposed improvements in the public right-of-way include six new street trees and two new class II bicycle parking racks on 3rd Street, and seven new street trees and one new class II bicycle parking rack on Ritch Street. A new 10-foot sidewalk would also be constructed along the project’s Ritch Street frontage. No diesel backup generators are proposed on-site. Construction of the proposed project is anticipated to take 12 months. Project construction would not entail any excavation, grading, or ground disturbance, except for the construction of the proposed sidewalks on 3rd Street and Ritch Street and 30 cubic yards of soil disturbance for an elevator pit. Construction equipment staging would primarily occur in the adjacent parking lot to the northwest of the subject building. Intermittent sidewalk or traffic lane closures may be required to move construction equipment and construct right-of-way improvements.

projects.name: 1200 Indiana Street
projects.description: Change of use and related tenant improvements in some portions of the existing structure, approx. 4,350 sf, which contains a Wholesale Storage use. The project, d.b.a. "Alaf Extracts," proposes conversion of approx. 250 sf to Light Manufacturing and approx. 250 sf to Cannabis Retail with accessory Parcel Delivery Service, and use of approx. 400 sf of the (e) Wholesale Storage. The remaining area of the structure and (e) Wholesale Storage use will remain unoccupied and unimproved. Cannabis Retail is permitted in PDR-1-G so long as (a) the establishment holds a valid Cannabis Microbusiness permit from the City’s Office of Cannabis, and (b) the Cannabis Retail Use occupies no more than 1/3 of the total floor area occupied by the PDR and Cannabis Retail Uses on the premises (PCS 210.3). Parcel Delivery Service may be an Accessory use for Cannabis Retail only (PCS 102).

projects.name: 50 08TH ST
projects.description: Conversion of 120 existing tourist hotel rooms to group housing rooms on floors 7, 8 and 9. No construction proposed.

projects.name: 1310 JUNIPERO SERRA BLVD
projects.description: The project proposes the construction of a one-story 23-foot-tall accessory maintenance and facility building for the San Francisco Golf Club (approximately 19,100 gross square feet.) The building will house administration offices for the maintenance staff, a repair shop for maintenance of vehicles and equipment, mowers, golf cart, staff break room and lockers/bathrooms. The Project includes a surface parking lot consisting of 23 parking spaces located at the rear of the proposed building.

projects.name: 1257 Guerrero St
projects.description: A Conditional Use Authorization for a B&B for five or fewer guest rooms within a Single-Family Dwelling was approved under CPC per Motion No. 19202. This CUA was never vested with a building permit and has expired meaning the legal use of the building is still a Single-Family Dwelling. Project proposes to legalize the current unpermitted Hotel Use for five or fewer guest rooms and obtain a building permit to vest the previously approved Conditional Use Authorization (CPC Motion No. 19202). To comply with Planning Code Enforcement 2025-007297ENF, no physical changes.

projects.name: 831 MONTGOMERY ST
projects.description: Certificate of Appropriateness request for work at adjoining properties 809, 831, and 845 Montgomery; 530 Jackson Street; and 100 Columbus Avenue. At 809 Montgomery Street, work includes installation of one new window at the secondary north elevation at the second floor, installation of a new skylight on the roof, and interior alterations related to internally merging this building with 831 Montgomery Street. At 831 Montgomery Street, work includes replacement of the non-historic brick-veneer cladding and storefront enframement at the Montgomery Street façade with new brick veneer cladding, replacement of the non-historic storefront infill and entrance security gate with new multilite steel-and-glass storefront infill, removal of a non-historic rear one-story addition, installation of a one-story rear exterior egress stair at the basement level leading to the ground level, installation of two new skylights, and interior alterations related to internally merging this building with 809 Montgomery Street. At 100 Columbus Avenue/845 Montgomery Street, work includes modification of the proposed previously approved steel-and-wood open rear egress stair, which is physically attached to the rear of 809 Montgomery Street but is located in the rear open areas of 845 Montgomery Street and 100 Columbus Avenue, to have a smaller overall footprint, incorporate an internal ADA chair lift, and add glass railings. At 530 Jackson Street, work includes replacement of seven non-historic aluminum and wood windows with new aluminum windows at the rear north elevation and the secondary west elevation in connection with fire safety requirements for the construction of the open rear egress stair for 809 Montgomery Street.

projects.name: 530 JACKSON STREET
projects.description: On Level 5, the existing exterior terrace will be renovated. The work includes replacing the two existing framed glass doors with sliding framed glass panels and adding a new cantilevered trellis, along with new planters and benches. The project also proposes replacing select portions of the existing non-historic stucco cladding at the south elevation of Level 5. The non-historic metal railing at the Level 5 terrace will be replaced and a skylight in the terrace floor will be removed/infilled. Select non-historic skylights at the roof will also be removed/infilled. The project will adhere to the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards and ensure the historic integrity of the building (Levels 1-4) is maintained. The proposed improvements will not affect or remove any of the building's character-defining features at Levels 1-4. Level 5 was added in 1998 and does not contain any character-defining features.

projects.name: 530 JACKSON ST
projects.description: Certificate of Appropriateness to permit replacing the existing non-historic storefronts at the ground floor with new compatible storefronts. The proposed storefronts will be compatible in materials and proportions. Additionally, the existing non-historic window units on the building's south (street facade) and west elevations (floors 2 - 5) will be replaced. The existing painted brick surface on the south elevation will be repainted. All historic features of the building will be retained and protected. The project will adhere to the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards and ensure the historic integrity of the building is maintained. The proposed improvements will not affect or remove any of the structure's character-defining features.

projects.name: CCDC - 949 Grant Avenue
projects.description: This project proposes to expand its occupancy to all three floors of the building: the basement, ground floor, and all of the second floor, which will increase its use size from 2,500 sq. ft. to 4,340 sq. ft. The expansion of use will not result in any change in use; CCDC will continue to use the space for community service purposes. The use size of 4,340 sq. ft. requires a Conditional Use Authorization because it exceeds the use size limit of 2,500 sq. ft. for the Chinatown Visitor Retail District pursuant to Sec. 121.4 of the SF Planning Code.

projects.name: 450 PACIFIC AVENUE
projects.description: The proposed project at 450 Pacific Avenue consists of improvements to support its continued office use; remove the existing metal fencing and gate along Pacific Avenue, the non-historic storefront and entry, and the metal gratings in front of many windows along the building’s Osgood Place frontage. New storefront systems and an entry would be installed within the same building openings, though at the approximate location of the existing fencing rather than at the setback storefront, and the windows along Osgood would remain unobscured.

projects.name: 900 Sansome Street
projects.description: The proposed project would convert the existing two-story (above basement) 28,863-square-foot parking garage on the site to office use, including a new elevator, building entrance, and bathroom upgrades. The building was constructed in 1927 and is located within the Northeast Waterfront Historic District. The project would include minor interior and exterior modifications including replacing the ground floor on the first level (removing vehicle ramps and replacing with concrete flooring to match existing floors at grade), replacing the windows on the first level to match the existing second story windows, constructing a new entryway with an awning, and removing two roll-up doors and replacing them with windows and bulkheads to match the existing facade. The project would require approximately 18 cubic yards of soil excavation for the elevator pit. The existing building envelope would remain the same. The project would include 6 class 1 bicycle parking spaces in a storage room as well as two off-street vehicle parking spaces on the basement level. On Sansome Street, two existing curb cuts would be replaced with improved sidewalk. The north-most existing curb cut on Sansome Street would be retained to access the two vehicle parking spaces on the basement level of the building. The project will also include removal of the existing steel windows at the non-visible rear east elevation and installation of new fire-rated metal windows in the slightly modified existing openings.

projects.name: 334 ELLIS STREET
projects.description: Construction of a new seven-story building with a single-level, below-grade basement (no parking proposed) on an existing surface lot at 334 Ellis Street. The primary use is social services to support the GLIDE Foundation's various community programs. The 334 Ellis lot will be merged with the adjacent 330 Ellis and 302 Ellis lots to become a corner lot. GLIDE intends to use all three buildings for social services and horizontally connect 334 with 330 Ellis on the upper floors in the future to aid with unifying the various social services that they offer.

projects.name: 3400 LAGUNA ST
projects.description: The approximately 68,090-square-foot (1.6-acre) project site at 3400 Laguna Street in the Marina neighborhood is currently improved with five buildings and contains a Planning Code Article 10 Landmark (Ladies' Protection and Relief Society, Landmark No. 320). The project site has been occupied by the Heritage on the Marina residential care retirement community since 1925. The proposed project would demolish two of the five existing buildings (the Perry Connector and the Health Care Center) and construct two new buildings (the Bay Building and the Francisco Building) of heights not to exceed 40 feet and in the same locations as the demolished structures. The proposed project would renovate two of the other three existing buildings on the site and make improvements to the Julia Morgan Building. In total, the proposed project would add approximately 58,380 square feet of institutional use, a new driveway and curb cut, a below grade parking garage, a new loading dock, and accessible off-street passenger loading. The proposal would increase the number of residential care suites by 23 from 86 to 109. The proposed project would continue to operate as a residential care facility.

projects.name: 1499 WEBSTER STREET
projects.description: Expansion of the existing dialysis clinic to provide a new accessible entry into the tenant improvement space. The existing dialysis clinic has 30 patient stations. To connect the adjacent tenant space to the existing clinic, two patient stations will be removed. No change of use is proposed.

projects.name: 27 VAN NESS AVE
projects.description: Minor Permit to Alter for the San Francisco Department of Public Health (DPH) plan to move the Adult Immunization & Travel Clinic (AITC) from its current location at 101 Grove Street to the ground floor of 27 Van Ness Avenue, which is the first floor suite of 25 Van Ness Avenue. Planned work will modify the 2,500 square foot interior space to provide a public-facing waiting area, injection rooms, and staff work areas. This will involve the partial demolition of existing interior walls, flooring and partial ceiling areas in the offices and restrooms. New walls, flooring, suspended/gypsum board ceiling system, new casework and interior transaction windows will be added. Related mechanical, plumbing, fire protection and electrical work will also be performed. The existing structural system will remain without major modifications and the project contains no seismic retrofit scope.

projects.name: 2870-2880 California Street
projects.description: Voluntary structural improvement on first floor and basement levels, including a new storage. New ADA ramp inside storefront in compliance with ABE program, including two new unisex restrooms, one janitor closet, kitchenette, and create a 1-hour rated hallway and a 1-hour rated exit passageway as a second egress. Proposed work also includes removal of existing rear brick wall and the replacement of all rear windows and doors.

projects.name: SFVAMC Fort Miley
projects.description: Tracking record for SFVAMC Fort Miley Campus Alternative 1 Construction 2013-2020. SFVAMC will modernize existing facilities; retrofit or replace seismically threatened buildings, create new structures that house patient care, education, administrative, hospital & research functions, and provide increased parking for Veterans, staff members, and visitors.

projects.name: NonRetail 221 MAIN ST
projects.description: The project site at 221 Main Street (Block 3740/034) has a lot area of 16,912 square feet and fronts Main Street and Spear Street between Folsom and Howard Streets in downtown San Francisco (the “Property”). The Property is in the C-3-0(SD) zoning district, 200-S height and bulk district, and the Transit Center Special Sign District. The site is currently developed with a 16-story building that is primarily utilized as office space above the ground floor. The ground floor of the Property is elevated significantly above street level. The uses on the ground floor consist of tenant amenities and a vacant commercial space on the Spear Street frontage, most recently occupied by a child care use. The vacant commercial space, Suite 103, is elevated approximately 4'-11" above street level with entry doors set back approximately 45'-4.5" from the edge of the sidewalk. The project proposes to establish a 4,492 square feet non-retail fitness center at the ground floor in Suite 103 as well as a new building-common lactation room to serve tenants of the Property (the “Project”). To establish the proposed use, the Project requires a change of use from child care facility to office use. The Project seeks Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code sections 303 and 210.2 to establish a Non-Retail Sales and Service use at the ground floor.

projects.name: 462 Bryant Street
projects.description: The proposed project is to add five (5) stories of office as well as a green roof and a commonly-accessible rooftop deck. The first-floor office and basement-level will remain. Currently, the Project site contains 13,505 gross square feet ("gsf") off office use, 9,965 gsf of which will remain. The 3, 540 gsf mezzanine level currently used as office is proposed to be eliminated. The Project will add 49,995 gsf of office at the site, for a total of 63,239 gsf of office. Although the Project will eliminate two off-street parking spaces int he basement, the Property's off-street service vehicle spaces will remain.

projects.name: 474 Bryant Street
projects.description: The project includes demolition of two vacant Production, Distribution and Repair (PDR) buildings (collectively measuring 22,842 gross square feet), adjusting the existing lot line, to accommodate two separate projects, the Project and a separate project to be located at 77 Stillman Street, on two separate parcels (each parcel will measure 8,622 gross square feet). The Project (consisting of one seven-story, 85-foot tall, mixed use building located at 474 Bryant Street) will consist of up to 49,999 square feet of Office use on the upper six floors over approximately 8,566 square feet of Light Manufacturing use on the ground floor and a basement garage. The garage includes 6 parking and loading spaces for the proposed PDR use. A total of 36 Class 1 and four Class 2 bicycle parking spaces are provided.

The Project (consisting of a seven-story, 85-foot tall, mixed-use building located at 77 Stillman Street) will consist of 49,834 square feet of Office use on the upper six floors over approximately 8,566 square feet of Light Manufacturing use on the ground floor and a basement garage. The garage includes 14 parking spaces for office tenants and 6 parking and loading spaces for the proposed PDR use. A total of 36 Class 1 and four Class 2 bicycle parking spaces are provided.

projects.name: SFMTA_1200 15th St Rehabilitation
projects.description: The proposed project would renovate, rehabilitate, and seismically retrofit the existing 29,500-square-foot historic building at 1200 15th Street to provide office and operational space for use by the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) Parking and Traffic Enforcement Division. The project would also install one temporary trailer (size to be determined) to house the division’s emergency-related operations. Six electric vehicle (EV) parking spaces with EV charging stations would be installed on the ground floor of the existing building and 34 electric bike parking spaces with charging stations would be installed in the yard to accommodate SFMTA fleet vehicles. The project would add 425 public employees to the site. The project would include streetscape improvements around the site. See plans dated April 29, 2022 (site plan revision 01). Project construction would be managed by San Francisco Public Works (PW) and would incorporate the PW standard construction measures as indicated. See attached project description memo for full project description.

projects.name: 200 RHODE ISLAND STREET
projects.description: The Property contains a five-story 1912 building with a three-story and a two-story addition. The Project Sponsor is currently seeking Article 10 Landmark designation for the Property. Once designated, the Property becomes eligible for the Vertical Controls for Office Uses pursuant to Planning Code Sections 210.3B and 803.9(f). The proposed project entails a change in use from PDR (Production, Distribution and Repair) to office use on the third and fourth floors (totaling approximately 22,580 square feet), The Zoning Administrator has determined that there is 12,333 sf of existing, legal non-conforming office space at the building of which 9,655 square feet will be shifted to the fifth floor and 2,007 sf will be shifted to the third floor.

projects.name: 151-199 POTRERO AVENUE

The existing 2,650-square-foot Building B is proposed to be demolished and replaced with a 9,012-square-foot building that would be tied into the adjacent Buildings A and C. Approximately 13,448 square feet of existing space on the fourth and fifth floors of Buildings C and E would be converted from Light Manufacturing to General Entertainment use. The proposed project also includes the following: renovation of Buildings A, C, and E, specifically interior alterations throughout; installation of new off-street parking spaces accessed from 15th Street; and new storefront and entrance systems.

The proposed EV chargers would be installed either within the existing building (without requiring any excavation) or in the parking lot (also without excavation or with minimal amount of removal of the existing asphalt), or both.

projects.description: New construction of a one-story warehouse building approximately 48 1/2 feet by 160 feet, 7,760 square feet, and 30 feet tall at the south side of the site. The building would include warehouse space, work room, and restrooms. There are a total of 7 existing parking spaces and 1 existing accessible/van parking space. The project would add an additional 17 parking spaces (13 off of 23rd Street adjacent to the existing office building and 4 adjacent to the proposed building), for a total of 24 parking spaces. projects.description: Add 1 new exterior metal storage rack with roof covering.

projects.name: 2200 KEITH STREET
projects.description: The project scope consists of tenant improvements to an existing office/warehouse including a buildout of the 2nd level for an open warehouse area and a new stair to the new 2nd floor office and storage area. No exterior, foundation, or structural work is proposed.

projects.name: 1901 JERROLD AVENUE (1900 KIRKWOOD AVENUE)
projects.description: The Project consists of the redevelopment of the SF Market campus' southeast quadrant lot in the Bayview neighborhood of San Francisco. The general scope of the Project is the demolition of the existing warehouse, dock, and site components and construction of a new core and shell warehouse which will be a produce and food-handling facility. The project will include PDR for use by future tenants, a small operations area, and a food recovery center. The Project also includes on-site horizontal improvements and off-site improvements. The project site is located on a lot (final Parcel Map is submitted) by Kirkwood Avenue to the south and Rankin Street to the east. The site is bound on the north and west by the Marshalling Yard. The former Jerrold Avenue (to the north) and Selby Street (to the west) right-of-ways are vacated and will be a part of the SF Market marshaling yard via the Parcel Map referenced above. The project site is currently occupied by a two-level warehouse with loading dock. The horizontal improvements include both onsite and offsite construction. Onsite improvements include utilities, paving and grading, parking and accessible ramps, and storm water provisions. Offsite improvements include the construction of new sidewalks, curbs, gutter, street lighting, planting of street trees, and replacement of street paving where required for utility connections. The vertical improvements include the construction of one building. The building is a one-story, type V-B, fully sprinklered building with approximately 67,222 sq. ft. of gross building area. The building is approximately 40'-0" to the highest point of the roof.

projects.name: 749 Toland Street & 2000 McKinnon Avenue
projects.description: Four buildings are proposed on the two lots with a truck court between the four structures. Buildings A & B are 4-story structures providing 28' clear dock high industrial space. this industrial space contains a partial level of office located above the loading door. Above the 36' level is general parking for employees and visitors. The level above this contains upper level (UL) industrial. This UL industrial has a 14' high clear space and is served via a common loading dock on the ground level and service elevators. Buildings C & D are two story structures providing 28' clear dock high industrial space. Each building has a partial level of office located above the loading doors.

projects.name: 301 TOLAND ST
projects.description: The project proposes to convert 301 Toland to a Private Parking Garage for use as employee parking for Waymo's existing automotive maintenance site at 201 Toland. The proposal includes a break room for employees, security office, small meeting rooms, and restrooms. Work includes tenant improvements to provide a new vehicle ramp, new walls, millwork, ceilings, finishes, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC. The proposal would convert the existing wholesale sales/storage use to Private Parking Garage use.

projects.name: 1723 & 1727 WALLACE AVE

projects.name: 655 BROTHERHOOD WAY
projects.description: The Project would include: (1) modification to the blue-top yard at the front of the site; (2) addition of a single-story structure at the front of the existing building, within a portion of the existing blue-top play yard; (3) modification of an existing play area at the southeast corner of the site and within an existing fenced area; (4) modification of an existing central courtyard play area; and (5) modification of a classroom within the existing gymnasium building to create a kitchen area for on-site food preparation. The Project would further increase the maximum allowable student enrollment from 396 to 436. All four existing on-site street vehicular parking spaces will remain, and additional vehicular parking will continue to be provided per private agreement with neighboring property owner on surface parking lot to east. projects.name: EVP 855 GEARY ST - E parking
projects.description: Conditional Use Application request for a change of use to establish 20 parking spaces and 20 car chargers on the ground floor of the building for private parking and electric vehicle (“EV”) charging for its autonomous vehicle rideshare fleet (the “Project”). Upgrades to the building would include adding EV charging equipment and accompanying electrical gear, upgrades to the existing bathrooms and employee amenity space, the addition of a sprinkler system, and ADA upgrades. The existing curb cuts would be maintained and no substantial changes to the building exterior are proposed. 855 Geary will be an important base of operations for Cruise’s all-electric fleet as it is centrally located in the city and will minimize deadhead miles by providing rideshare vehicles a place to park and charge that is close to rider demand. The Project requires conditional use authorization for a Private Parking Garage use and Utility Installation in order to convert the ground floor spaces to private use and install EV charging equipment for those spaces. The existing private parking on the basement and second levels would be maintained.

projects.name: 2350 GREEN ST
projects.description: The 37,734-square-foot (sf) project site contains an existing K-8 school (St Vincent De Paul School), which is located on a block bounded by Green, Pierce, Steiner and Union streets. The project site is part of the St. Vincent de Paul California Parish Complex, which includes three buildings; the main school building (currently used as the lower school) constructed in 1924; and the Gymnasium and classroom buildings (currently used as the middle school) constructed in 1948. The lower school building is 39’-4” tall and 18,856 sf and the middle school building is 42’-4” tall and 5,972 sf. The corner of the site is now a surface parking lot with 25 off-street spaces. The courtyard is also used for parking, with 7 spaces in a carport at grade under the middle school and approximately 10 additional non-striped spaces in the courtyard. The Parish Complex is considered an individual historic resource. The proposed project includes infill of the first floor of the middle school, and a new addition, including a new stairway connecting the middle school and the lower school. These additions would expand the existing building footprint. The middle school would increase in size from 5,972 sf to 13,650 sf for an increase of 7,678 sf. The building renovation would involve seismic upgrades to the middle school building, and the new addition to the middle school building to connect to the lower school. With the ground floor infill of the middle school, the parking area at the main courtyard would be reduced from 17 to 7 parking spaces. The project would also rehabilitate the existing lower school building. Demolition would include infill of an existing carport, and demolition of the existing west stair tower at the lower school, which would reduce the size of the lower school building from 18,856 sf to 17,028 sf for a net reduction of 1,828 sf. The gym would be reduced in size from 22,579 sf to 21,910 sf for a net reduction of 669 sf. The total net change for the buildings would be an additional 5,181 sf, and the heights of the buildings would remain unchanged. The existing parking lot at the corner of Green and Pierce streets would remain, however, the project also includes the construction of a 7,820 sf elevated play area above the existing surface parking. The elevated play area would range in height from 8’ to 11’-4”. The project would also involve the removal of one curb cut along Green Street in order to provide a new pedestrian ramp to access the proposed new entry. Together, the existing school buildings are currently 47,407 sf and would be expanded by 5,181 sf for a new total area of 52,588 sf. The project involves building demolition of 3,088 sf, and new building infill and an expanded building footprint of 8,269 sf. The basement area is located under the gym and middle school buildings and is currently 15,867 sf and would be expanded by 36 sf to a new area of 15,903 sf. Current enrollment at the school would remain unchanged at 360 students. The proposed project excavation would require 215 cubic yards (cy) cut, 583 cy fill, for a total import of 368 cy. Approximately 5 feet of fill would be added to the main courtyard bringing the finished grade to approximately 82 feet. Excavation of 5 to 10 feet of soil is anticipated for rehabilitation related to the expansion of the basement area. The new building addition would be supported on a drilled pier foundation. These piers would be cast-in-place straight shaft friction piers, with a minimum diameter of 18 inches and extend a minimum of 30 feet below grade, into dense sand or stiff clay. Construction of the proposed project would last approximately twelve months.

projects.name: 2001 VAN NESS AVE
projects.description: Change of Use from Office Space (1,940SF) to Medical Office use (Allergy Testing Facility).

projects.name: 2031 Bush St
projects.description: Phased project that includes voluntary seismic upgrade, mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems upgrades, and accessibility improvements. Exterior work includes new raised exterior walkway with storage and utility rooms below, exterior entry stair, elevator tower and control room, roofing, window rehabilitation and replacement, sump pumps and rear yard paving. Select interior renovations include new mechanical equipment, electrical panels, and sprinklers, in addition to replacement of the existing mezzanine, restrooms and kitchen.

projects.name: 201 VAN NESS AVENUE
projects.description: The Symphony is exploring potential improvements to the existing 210,000 gross sq. ft. Davies Symphony Hall. This preliminary application proposes to renovate the Hall and explore expansion of the street level lobby, a new performance park, a new recital hall, an expanded musician support wing, and interior renovations of the main concert hall with a net addition of approximately 55,000 gross sq. ft. of floor area. The existing and proposed uses would remain public uses consistent with the Property’s P (Public) zoning designation. The scenario presented in this application would decrease seating capacity in the main concert hall from 2,700 seats to approximately 2,100 seats while adding 400 seats in a new recital hall at the corner of Van Ness Avenue and Hayes Street. Open space areas would increase from approximately 4,600 sq. ft. to approx. 39,000 sq. ft, with several new outdoor terraces. The existing 60-space surface parking lot at Franklin and Grove Streets would be constructed with an outdoor performance park, including building areas for event activities and two below-grade parking levels with 76 parking spaces accessible from Franklin. Two off-street freight loading spaces would be provided off of Franklin and the existing freight loading space along Hayes would be eliminated. No changes are proposed to the existing Zellerbach Hall. As a public structure, the project would also be subject to the Arts Commission’s Civic Design Review per City Charter Sec. 5.103.

projects.name: 660 OAK ST
projects.description: Conduit Intelligence PBC requests Planning Department approval for a low-impact headquarters use within the existing historic building at 660 Oak Street. The building is part of the Sacred Heart Parish Complex, Landmark No. 316. The project seeks Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code Sections 202.11 and 303 to allow adaptive reuse of the historic building for Conduit’s headquarters operations, including professional, administrative, research and development, design, and related startup office functions. The project does not propose demolition, new construction, expansion of the building envelope, or a public-facing retail use. Conduit’s operations will be primarily office-based and conducted inside the existing building.

projects.name: 2245 - 2255 POST ST
projects.description: This project proposes a new building to replace the existing buildings on two adjoining sites for the new home of the JFCS Holocaust Center. The building will contain rooms for public exhibitions, a lecture hall, library, classrooms, offices and conference spaces as well as the Holocaust Center's archives. This is a new proposal for the Holocaust Center which will replace the previously approved project, because the project sponsor acquired the adjacent property, more than doubling the size of the proposed facility. This project will require a CUA for a non-residential building greater than 6,000 sf in gross floor area. The project sponsor seeks a Legislative Amendment to establish a Special Use District for this site to accommodate its program. The project sponsor will also apply for a lot merger of 2245 and 2255 Post Street.

projects.name: 270 MASONIC ST
projects.description: The proposal is for a Conditional Use Authorization, pursuant to Planning Code Sections 209.2 and 303(c) to convert the existing blood donation center (a medical service/health service use under the Planning Code) to a post-secondary educational institution use for the University of San Francisco. The project would include interior alterations to convert the existing blood collection center, laboratory facilities, and library uses to accommodate USF post-secondary educational institution uses such as academic instructional labs, classrooms, meeting and seminar rooms, and faculty/staff offices. The project would also include minor exterior alterations to the Blood Center building façade and signage. The project proposes minor reconfigurations of the existing parking lot to improve on-site circulation and ingress and egress for pedestrians, bicycles, and vehicles. No off-street parking spaces or floor area would be added.

projects.name: 1300 SHRADER ST
projects.description: An adaptive reuse and vertical addition are proposed to an existing one-story-over-basement building. A childcare facility serving approximately 38 children will be established and will include an outdoor play area. The two existing residential dwelling units will remain. One existing dwelling unit will remain substantially in place, and the second dwelling unit will be relocated to the basement level. The project includes interior renovations, excavation at the basement level, new egress stairs, and streetscape improvements.

projects.name: 1331-1333 NORIEGA STREET
projects.description: The project proposes a remodel of the existing two-story commercial building (dental office), including a horizontal addition. No change of use is proposed.

projects.description: COMMERCIAL TENANT IMPROVEMENT IN A SINGLE TENANT BUILDING ON FLOORS: BASEMENT, GROUND & MEZZ. projects.name: 380 LAGUNA HONDA BLVD
projects.description: The Department of Elections (Department) is requesting approval to install a ballot drop-off box near MUNI’s Forest Hill Station. The proposed drop box at the Forest Hill Station will be one of 34 boxes installed throughout the City. The purpose of the drop box is to provide a convenient, secure method for voters to deliver their ballots to the Department during each election. The Department identified this location based on criteria set by California Elections Code Section 4005, which emphasizes that drop-off boxes be located near public transportation. Election law also requires the Department to also consider local traffic patterns and limits to the types of transportation available to voters that could impede their access to a drop-off box. Voters often travel past the Station due to the topography and street infrastructure in the area surrounding this location. This common pathway will allow voters in the area to observe the drop-off box and utilize its availability. The ease of pedestrian access to the location will also facilitate and encourage voters to return their ballots using the drop-off location. Since the Forest Hill Station is a San Francisco Designated Landmark, per request from SF Planning, the Department is submitting a separate stand-alone application for the drop box at Forest Hill Station.

projects.description: Third floor vertical addition for commercial space. New third floor level deck. Fire sprinklers per nfpa13 and fire alarm deferred submittal. Facade alterations not included.

projects.name: Rintaro · kitchen & seating expansion
projects.description: The Zoning for this Property is PDR-1-G existing. Under this zoning, Rintaro is an existing Restaurant use, originally built in 2014 and under continuous operation by the same Owner. The current proposed construction is to add a Vertical Addition, second floor which is not seen from the street and is located to the rear of the property. There is Proposed Demolition of an rear facing existing porch at ground level = 96.5 SF, abutting a blank concrete wall of Rainbow Grocery. The New Second Floor Proposed Addition is = 893.6 SF. The purpose of the proposed second level is to primarily add Storage, kitchen expansion and 18 seats. Rintaro has added a Catering program, for Bento Boxes, sold by Table 22, that currently is 20% of the Owner's business revenue. See attached Square Footage Matrix for breakdown of Sq Ft. The Vertical Addition Proposed is within the height and bulk limits; is within the Maher area, but will require 10.8 CY excavation, and is exempt for < 50 CY. The revised Restaurant use only is less than 2500 SF. RESTAURANT USE = 2449.92 SF and CATERING USE = 439.08 SF. Zero lot lines are allowed within the PDR-1-G area. No variance, conditional uses area necessary, and the proposed project is within what is allowable under PDR-1-G zoning.
projects.summary: The existing Japanese restaurant proposes a rear second-floor addition for kitchen and storage space, plus 18 seats. Rintaro is already operating; the expansion completion date is not published.

projects.name: 333 DOLORES ST
projects.description: Conditional Use Authorization for the replacement of three temporary preschool portables on an existing preschool through 4th grade campus, with a new permanent building, and associated site improvements. The proposed project would remove three non-contributing temporary portables that house the preschool program for Children’s Day School. These structures are on a city legislated time clock to be replaced, most recently by Historic Preservation Commission Motion No. 0396, and Planning Commission Motion No. 20562. The replacement would consist of the construction of a single-story building (12 feet tall) with a roof deck on a site with an existing school building (to remain). The new building would house 7,995 square feet of classroom and administration space.

projects.name: 3250-70 18th St.
projects.description: The project site is the existing campus of the La Scuola International School at 3250 18th Street. The site is developed with a two-story over basement building known as the St. Charles building, three temporary portable buildings, and a recreational play yard for students at the school. In 2021, a second building on-site (3270 18th Street) was demolished and replaced with three temporary portable buildings. The portable classroom structures were installed on the site pursuant to the Mayor's Executive Directive on schools (Planning Department case no. 2021-006259PRJ). The La Scuola International School has a second campus building located at 741 South Van Ness Avenue; however, no changes are currently proposed for that campus building and La Scuola International School in this document refers to the campus at 3250 18th Street only. The project proposes to remove the three existing portable buildings and to construct a new four-story, 20,370-square-foot building in the southwestern portion of the existing play yard. The new building would be 59 feet tall (approximately 68 feet tall including rooftop appurtenances) and would include nine new classrooms, offices, a dining and kitchen area, an occupied roof, and other support spaces. The proposed project would increase maximum student enrollment for the K-8 school from 191 to 475 students and increase the number of teachers and staff from 54 to 96. Additionally, the existing play yard would be reconfigured and would change from 5,223 square feet to 9,681 square feet. In combination with the proposed 1,895-square-foot rooftop open space area and 652-square-foot outdoor deck on the new building, the proposed project would provide 12,228 total square feet of recreational open space. Other project elements include 36 class 1 bicycle parking spaces, 14 class 2 bicycle parking spaces, three new street trees on Shotwell Street, and a new ADA-compliant curb cut on 18th Street to provide pedestrian access to the primary entrance on 18th Street. In addition, sidewalk sections along the project’s frontages on 18th and Shotwell streets would be replaced. The project frontages on 18th and Shotwell streets are currently designated as passenger loading zones during school drop-off and pick-up hours on weekdays between 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and between 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.; no changes to the existing curb configuration are currently proposed. The proposed building would be supported by a mat foundation on improved soil. Approximately 7,600 square feet of soil would be disturbed. The mat-slab foundation would be supported by micro-piles and direct drilled sand-cement piles. No soil would be excavated or filled under the new mat-slab foundation. The ground surfaces immediately surrounding the building to the north and east would be raised by 3 feet. Project construction is anticipated to last 24 months.

projects.name: Pier 92 Modernization and Plant Replacement Project
projects.address: Pier 92 Modernization and Plant Replacement Project
projects.description: Martin Marietta seeks to modernize and reconstruct its existing sand processing facility at Pier 92 by installing new equipment, constructing a new warehouse, paving and reconfiguring the site, and installing a new modern stormwater management system. No changes are proposed to Pier 92 infrastructure or facilities located outside of the project site’s boundaries. The essential nature of the existing operations at the facility would not change. Rather, the proposed project would allow for the existing operation to continue on a redesigned site with modern equipment and improved environmental controls. To accommodate these changes, the project proposes to increase the site footprint from 190,229 square feet to 224,600 square feet under a new lease with the Port of San Francisco. The project has also applied for a permit to construct/permit to operate from the Air District, which would allow the facility to process up to 800,000 US tons of sand per year. Construction of the project would take up to 7 months. Facility operations would continue during construction.

projects.name: 1225 VAN DYKE AVE
projects.description: The project consists of the merger of Assessor's Parcel Numbers (APNs) 4827-003 and 4827-001, located at 1225 and 1205 Van Dyke Avenue, respectively, to allow continued operation and consolidation of an existing construction and demolition debris (CDI) transfer/processing facility and junk yard operation. Both parcels are developed industrial properties located within an established industrial area. Prior to vacating the site, the former tenant at 1205 Van Dyke Avenue operated a permitted junk yard and conducted material handling activities similar in nature to those currently conducted at 1225 Van Dyke Avenue. The project would continue the existing receipt, sorting, processing, storage, and transfer of construction and demolition debris (CDI), including concrete, dirt, wood, metals, cardboard, copper wire, aluminum, and limited quantities of plastic. Materials would continue to be stored outdoors within designated stockpile areas. The project does not involve the development of previously undeveloped land or the introduction of a new land use. Rather, the project would consolidate operations across two existing industrial parcels that have historically supported similar material recovery, storage, processing, and salvage activities. Vehicles delivering CDI would continue to enter the facility from Van Dyke Avenue, proceed to a scale for weighing and load inspection, unload materials in designated areas, and be weighed upon departure to obtain tare weight before exiting the site. Operations would continue to utilize existing material handling and processing equipment, including 226B and 246C skid steers, a Hitachi EX120-5 excavator, and 924G and 938M wheel loaders. The existing facility at 1225 Van Dyke Avenue currently processes less than 87.2 tons of material per day. Following consolidation of the two industrial parcels, the facility would operate as a medium-volume CDI transfer/processing facility with a permitted throughput of up to 166.38 tons per day. To support operational efficiency, the project includes installation of a second truck scale and operation of a shredder to process material suitable for Alternative Daily Cover (ADC), a material used at permitted municipal solid waste landfills in lieu of earthen cover. The project represents the continued operation and consolidation of existing industrial and material recovery activities on developed parcels that have historically supported similar uses. No substantial alteration of the existing site configuration is proposed, and no new buildings or expansion into undeveloped areas would occur.

projects.name: 2 STOCKTON ST
projects.description: The project site is located on the corner of Stockton and Market streets. The project block is bounded by Stockton Street to the west, Market Street to the south, Ellis Street to the southwest and O’Farrell Street to the north. Buildings adjacent to the project site include a six-story-over-basement commercial building to the north (48 Stockton), and the historic ten-story commercial Phelan Building to the east. The existing building at 2 Stockton Street is a four-story-over-basement steel-framed building with retail uses on the first three floors (encompassing a total of approximately 71,700 gross square feet) and storage uses on the fourth floor. Originally constructed in 1907 as the retail store, Roos Bros., the 2 Stockton building was remodeled in 1994 to become the Virgin MegaStore. The existing building has been vacant since early 2020; however, one retailer is slated to occupy a portion of the building beginning in 2022 through September 2023. The project site is zoned as Downtown Retail (C-3-R) and is in a 80-130-F height and bulk district. The building is identified as an Article 11 Preservation Designation “Category V – Unrated Building” within the Kearny Market Mason Sutter Conservation District. The proposed project consists of constructing 49,999 square feet of office uses through the demolition and expansion of the existing fourth floor and the addition of a fifth, sixth, and partial seventh floor to the existing four-story-over-basement building. Retail use would be located on the first three floors and basement of the building and the upper four floors would be designated for office uses. The top three floors would be set back from the adjacent Phelan building approximately 19 feet. The building roof would contain mechanical equipment, emergency generator, electrical rooms, an elevator, and 2,488 square feet of solar photovoltaic panels. In addition to retail uses, the basement would contain building services and operations, a bicycle commuter facility with 16 Class I bicycle parking spaces, clothing lockers, and shower facilities serving both retail and office uses. No on site or off site parking would be provided. The proposed project would install 14 Class II bicycle parking spaces along the Stockton and Market Streets sidewalks. The three existing street trees along the project frontage on Market Street would not be removed. No streetscape improvements are anticipated.

The ground floor of the Property consists of twenty-six tenant spaces, with retail sales commercial uses, including restaurants, cafes, salon, bank, and fitness center, and nine vacant tenant spaces, two of which including the subject space have Spear Street frontage. The subject tenant space has been vacant since September 2021. The subject tenant space was last occupied by a real estate brokerage office for approximately eighteen months. Prior to the real estate leasing office, the subject space sat dark for approximately eighteen months after a long-term dental office (Findlay Dental Arts) ceased operations. The subject tenant space is directly adjacent to an existing retail fitness center and from the pedestrian experience on Spear Street will appear as if an extension of that adjacent retail fitness center. To establish the proposed use, the Project requires a change of use from real estate brokerage office (a Retail Sales and Service Use) to Office Use (fitness center serving the upper floor office tenant). The Project seeks Conditional Use authorization pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 210.2 to establish a Non-Retail Sales and Service use at the ground floor. * Please note, for clarity, the Project and Land Use Table below only includes information pertaining to the ground floor.

projects.name: 345 Spear Street & 2 Harrison Street
projects.description: The project scope consists of a change of use within the existing ground-floor commercial spaces, converting retail space into office use with associated tenant improvements. The project would be reviewed per Planning Code Section 803.9(4) for the Article 10 Landmark and will require review by the Historic Preservation Commission to ensure compliance with the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation. The project also includes architectural and signage upgrades at eight existing ground-floor entry vestibules within the Hills Plaza complex—identified as the Events, .Org, Lobby, and Fitness entries. The project encompasses four distinct vestibule types, represented across eight entry locations within the complex. The project will maintain the character-defining features of the building while activating the ground floor with viable, long-term uses. There will be no changes to the building’s massing, height, or footprint. No demolition, expansion, or structural modifications to the building envelope are proposed. All proposed work will occur within the existing building envelope and within the existing plaza-level storefront footprint.

projects.name: 345 SPEAR ST
projects.description: The project scope consists of a change of use of 12,172 sqft within the existing ground-floor commercial spaces, converting the existing retail space into office use, with associated tenant improvements. No exterior alterations are proposed, and there will be no changes to the building’s massing, height, or footprint. All proposed work will occur within the existing building envelope. The project will maintain the character-defining features of the building while activating the ground floor with a viable, long-term uses. No expansion of floor area, no new construction, and no exterior façade changes are proposed.

projects.name: 680 Folsom · office lounge conversion
projects.description: The project site at 680 Folsom Street (Block 3735, Lots 013 & 014) has a lot area of 37,195 sq. ft. and is located at the corner of Folsom and Hawthorne Streets in downtown San Francisco (the “Property”). The Property is in the C-3-S and C-3-0(SD) zoning districts, 320-I height and bulk district, and Transit Center Special Sign District. The site is currently developed with a 14-story building that is primarily utilized as office space above the ground floor. The ground floor of the Property is elevated above street level and set back from the frontage along Folsom Street. The uses on the ground floor consist of tenant amenities and commercial space, including a vacant commercial space that was most recently occupied by a restaurant in 2020 (the “Vacant Suite”). The project proposes to establish a 2,094 sq. ft., non-retail office amenity space to be used as an employee lounge and shared conference room in the Vacant Suite at the Property (the “Project”). To establish the proposed use, the Project requires a change of use from retail to office use.
projects.summary: A vacant former restaurant would become a 2,094-square-foot lounge and shared conference space for office employees.

projects.name: 200 RHODE ISLAND STREET
projects.description: The project proposes to expand 12,333 sq. ft. of legal non-conforming office space at the ground floor to include a 1,059 sq. ft. area that is currently used as a vestibule and bathroom. The project would expand the legal non-conforming office use to 13,392 sq. ft. at the ground floor of the property, an increase of approximately 8.6% in area. No request for expansion of non-residential, non-conforming use has been previously requested for the property. A Conditional Use Authorization pursuant to Planning Code section 181(i) is required for the project.

projects.description: New construction of a Cannabis Wholesale Distribution facility (approx. 500sf).

projects.name: Mendell Plaza · proposed restaurant structure
projects.description: Variance request from Planning Code Section 145.1, which requires that 60% of the street frontages containing active uses be fenestrated with transparent windows and doors to provide visibility into the building. The proposed building use is as a small restaurant that sits on a triangular lot that faces Mendell Plaza, Oakdale Avenue and 3rd Street.
projects.summary: A small restaurant structure is proposed on the triangular site at Third and Oakdale, facing Mendell Plaza. No future operator or opening date verified.

projects.name: 1710 Church St
projects.description: The purpose of this project is to expand the amenities offered by Church Fitness. A sauna, cold plunge and rinsing station will be installed in the backyard of the gym. These three items will provide a greater opportunity for the gym's clientelle to enrich and promote their fitness and wellness goal. The expansion of the gym is a byproduct of members requesting the proposed amenities. The project will need to receive Conditional Use Authorization to convert backyard into an Outdoor Activity Area.

projects.name: 545 SANSOME ST
projects.description: Downtown Large Project Authorization for existing nine-story historic building with 55,759 square feet of office and 3,001 square feet of ground floor retail space. The Project proposes to demolish the adjacent single-story retail building at 501-505 Washington Street and a concrete capped, below-grade story at 517 Washington Street and construct a 49,999 square foot office addition (the “Project”). The new horizontal and penthouse addition would extend to the north and west of the Existing Building and would add 49,999 square feet of office space and 2,419 square feet of new ground floor retail. The principal historic street-facing facades of the Existing Building on Sansome and Mark Twain Place will be retained, and the addition has been carefully designed to respect and compliment the character of the preexisting structure. In total, the Project would result in a new building with 105,758 square feet of office and 5,420 square feet of ground floor retail. The Project will also provide 7,103 square feet of open space. 6,103 square feet of private open space would be provided for the building’s tenants, via a 1,245 square foot ground floor courtyard and a 4,858 square foot roof deck. In addition, the Project will add 1,000 square feet of POPOS, located at the ground level between the new structure and the adjacent Transamerica Redwood Park to the west. The new POPOS area will be designed as a visual extension of the existing Transamerica Redwood Park, while respecting the original character of the Park and the separation between the new and old.

projects.name: 712 MONTGOMERY ST
projects.description: Proposed project is to install an electric cable elevator from the first floor to the second floor. 1. This 5'x 5.5' cab elevator is to serve elderly and disable clients to have access to the property owner Collier Gwin second floor retail art gallery. This elevator is to serve only the second floor retail art gallery and no other tenants in the building. A 52"x 52" tow story elevator shaft will be built within the existing building envelope. No elevator penthouse will protrude above the existing building roof line. 2. Access to the elevator will be from a new exterior door at the Hotaling Alley at the rear of the building. An existing window at the Hotaling Alley will be enlarged to accommodate the new elevator lobby door. 3. The primary facade of the building and second floor entry stair access is from the Montgomery Street facade. No work will be done on this facade.

projects.name: Restaurant storefront works · 470 Pacific
projects.description: The proposed project is limited to the replacement of the three easternmost non-historic storefronts. The proposed storefronts will be built within the existing historic openings. No original fabric will be removed and the historic character of the building will be retained. The proposed storefront design will have full-height glass with vertical steel mullions that are rhythmically spaced. The storefront will also have a horizontal steel mullion at the location of a transom line and another horizontal steel mullion at the lower portion of the storefront. The panels below the lower horizontal mullion are proposed to be steel and will have the appearance of a bulkhead. The storefront will rest on the existing concrete base which is low in height. The entry door to the restaurant seating area will be located at the second bay from the east end and will be a framed door with a glazed panel. This portion of the storefront (7’-6” in length) will be set back to prevent the door from crossing the property line as it swings out. The third bay from the eastern end of the building will have an entry door to the restaurant’s kitchen. This door will be a solid metal door with a painted metal surround. The storefront glazing in this bay will be back-painted approximately halfway up the storefront to hide back of house storage. The proposed storefront will be compatible with the District through the use of painted steel, a material found throughout the Jackson Square Historic District. The new storefront design will also be compatible with its reference to both a bulkhead and transom line. The storefront mullions convey verticality, a characteristic that is compatible with typical punched windows in contributing buildings in the District.
projects.summary: The permit concerns replacement storefronts and restaurant entry doors in Jackson Square. It does not announce a new restaurant or confirm when this work will finish.

projects.name: 50 POST ST
projects.description: The project is a renovation of the Crocker Galleria, a retail facility located between Post and Sutter Streets. This includes the removal of escalators in the center of the atrium and installation of new vertical circulation elements (elevators and stairs) connecting all levels of the Galleria and the existing roof level POPOS. Work includes installation of base building infrastructure for new commercial cooking facilities, new mechanical and smoke control systems, new finishes and lighting throughout, and an enhanced external connection with the adjacent One Montgomery Tower office building. All levels will remain retail use and the proposed work is shell and core only in anticipation of retail uses. No increase in gross square footage or change of use is proposed.
