projects.description: The project proposes the adaptive reuse of an existing two-story, 14,320-square-foot commercial building at 3175 17th Street to house arts activities, dance studios, and support spaces for the Oberlin Dance Collective ("ODC"). In total, 9,074 square feet of Gross Floor Area is proposed for conversion from accessory freight loading, accessory parking, and retail floor areas to office use. Two existing garage doors and adjacent curb cuts would be removed, with infill façades to match the building’s existing façades along both street frontages. The Project would modify a third (existing) garage door fronting Tehama Street to accommodate 3 new service vehicle loading spaces, replacing 2 existing freight loading spaces. projects.name: Pier 70
projects.description: The proposed project would involve development of a 28-acre site into a mixed-use development, including parks, roads, and infrastructure. Below is a breakdown of the use types of the pier 70-waterfront site development. Residential – Development of a range of 2,000 to 1,000 new dwelling units consisting of approximately 1,712,000 - 903,000. As part of this residential program, Building 2 would be rehabilitated into approximately 120 dwelling units (consisting of approximately 110,000 gsf). Commercial Office – Construction of a range of 1,810,00 million gsf to 900,000 gsf of Class A Office and Research/Development space. As part of the commercial development, a portion of Building 12 would be rehabilitated into commercial office space (consisting of approximately 60,000 gsf). Retail and Arts – Construction of up to 400,000 gsf of new ground floor commercial retail and arts activity space, including small scale local production and small business incubator uses. Approximately 120,000 gsf of the retail and arts space would result from the construction of Buildings E-1A and E-1B, and approximately 115,000 gsf would result from the rehabilitation of Buildings 12 and 21. Parking – The proposal would provide parking within up to three newly-constructed district parking facilities and/or dispersed within buildings housing other uses, based upon the following maximum rates: o Residential Condominium Units: 1.0 space per dwelling unit; o Residential Rental Unit: 0.5 space per dwelling unit; o Commercial (includes office, restaurant, retail and arts, and all other uses): .9 spaces per 1,000 gsf of floor area Open Space and Recreation – The project includes construction of approximately seven acres of new public open space and recreational areas consisting of: approximately 3.9 acres for the Slipway Commons Waterfront Park; 0.6 acres for Market Square, located between Building 2 and 12; and, approximately 1.7 acres of useable rooftop open space on the district parking facilities. ¿ Infrastructure Development – The infrastructure development would include a) site preparation, including remediation of contaminated soils, grading, soil compaction and stabilization, construction and installation of water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, and utility infrastructure, and subsurface improvements to improve seismic conditions; and b) construction of streets and walkways, shoreline improvements, public access, and parks.

Lots A and B will be roughly rectangular shaped, will front onto Ortega Street, and will each contain a new single-family dwelling. Lot C will be a “L-shaped” flag lot and will contain the existing single-family residence that will be modified with new vertical and horizontal additions. Lot A would be 2,604 square feet, Lot B would be 2,532 square feet, and Lot C would be 4,142 square feet. The residence on Lot A would have four bedrooms and five bathrooms and would be approximately 3,753 square feet in size. The residence on Lot B would have three bedrooms and three bathrooms and would be 3,529 square feet in size with a two bedroom ADU. The residence on Lot C would have four bedrooms and three bathrooms and would be 3,596 square feet in size. Each single-family residence would be three stories (up to 23 feet above grade) and would have a two-car garage. In addition, the project would remove two existing significant trees on the project site but would add six new trees. Construction of the proposed project would excavate approximately 3,000 cubic yards of soil over an approximately 8,300 square-foot area to a depth of up to 25 feet below ground. projects.description: Demolition of a two-story single-family dwelling and erect a four-story, single-family dwelling unit with ADU.

projects.name: 3650 21ST ST
projects.description: Per SB-9, the project consists of the demolition of an existing three-story, single-family residence and construction of a new three-story-over-basement, two-unit residential building within the RH-1 Zoning District. There is a certificate of compliance application and new APN (3605/146) associated with the project; refer to DPW application (ID no. 12432).

projects.name: 701 San Bruno Avenue
projects.description: The project proposes the tantamount to demolition of the existing single-family dwelling and new construction of a 4-story building consisting of two dwelling units. The project scope includes a one-bedroom unit, garage and a TV room with a wet bar and full bathroom on the first floor, and a three bedroom unit on the second, third and fourth floors. The project provides one off-street parking space and two bicycle parking spaces, along with a new curb cut proposed off the 19th Street frontage. Each of the units are provided with access to the rear yard and code-compliant usable open space in the form pf patios and decks.

projects.name: 424 TEXAS ST
projects.description: The project proposes the demolition of an existing single-family home and the construction of a new single-family home and one-bedroom accessory dwelling unit (ADU) in its place. The new structure would consist of four stories. The ground floor would contain a new garage and a 612-square-foot ADU with one bedroom and separate living room and kitchen spaces. The second through fourth stories would contain the primary dwelling unit, which would include 4 bedrooms, 2.5 bathrooms, a sun room, and decks at the fourth floor and roof. The rear yard would be tiered and contain two patios, with one of the patios serving as private open space for the ADU.

projects.name: 4024 25TH STREET
projects.description: The project proposes the demolition of an existing two-story, single-family residence and construction of a new four-story, two-family residence within required setbacks and height limits. The project is in the Family Housing Opportunity Special Use District; a CUA for demolition is not required.

projects.name: 129 LAIDLEY ST
projects.description: The project proposes the demolition of an existing three-story, single-family residence and construction of a 26-foot-tall, four-story, single-family residence approximately 4,628 gross square feet. The proposed building would include an accessory dwelling unit (AUD) per California Government Code Section 65852.2. The project would require approximately 263 cubic yards of excavation.

projects.name: 654 28TH ST
projects.description: This project proposes demolition of an existing single-story building approximately 1,761 square feet with one Dwelling Unit and construction of a three-story, 3,998 square foot building with two Dwelling Units per SB 9.

projects.name: 1030 Francisco St
projects.description: The proposed project includes the removal of the existing 2-story single family residence. To be replaced by a new 3-story single family residence and attached ADU. The project replaces an outdated structure with a new multifamily building meeting current codes and the highest standards of current building practices.

projects.name: 2915 Vallejo Street
projects.description: Demolition of an existing 3-story over garage single-family home. Construction of a new 6-story single-family home and ADU.

projects.name: 170 Seacliff Avenue
projects.description: This project proposes a Conditional Use Authorization to demolish the existing residential structure pursuant to Section 317 and construct a new single-family residence at the Property. The property is in the RH-1(D) zoning district and 40-X height and bulk district. The existing building, built in 1914, requires structural improvements and other significant rehabilitative work. At the street, the dwelling will be aligned to one side of the lot, similarly located as the existing home, resulting in an improved and expanded side-by-side driveway with its neighbor, 178 Sea Cliff Avenue. The 170 and 178 Sea Cliff Avenue building will appear as two similar homes. The Project will meet the requirements of the California Green Building standards and San Francisco Green Building Amendments—endeavoring to maximize sustainability at the site.

projects.name: 428 15TH AVE
projects.description: Conditional Use Authorization request for demolition of a one-story, one-bedroom single-family house and the construction of a four-story residential building consisting of two three-bedroom units. The Project will also include an enclosed three-car garage and private open space for each unit.

projects.name: 276 Grand View Avenue
projects.description: Demolish existing two-story residential building. Excavate and enlarge existing basement. Construct a three-story, two-unit residential building with a two-car parking garage.

projects.name: 249 MISSISSIPPI ST
projects.description: New 2-Unit Building over Garage/Storage. Front Unit is a 324sf Studio, Rear Unit is a 2,476sf 3-Bedroom Apartment. The project calls for the demolition of an existing single-family structure and construction of a 2-Unit residence. The existing structure has been vacant for more than 5 years, is called abandoned in DBI permit history, and is in severe disrepair. The proposed 2-Unit building is modest in size and sensitively scaled at the street elevation to respond to the two adjacent houses.

projects.name: 146 MISSOURI ST
projects.description: Demolish the existing vacant, fire-damaged, two-story, single-family residential building and construct a new code-complying, seismically-sound, two-unit, four-story residential building. The structure will include a two-car garage on the ground floor, each unit will feature four bedrooms and 3.5 baths, and Unit 2 (upper unit) will include a roof deck. Excavation of 28 cubic yards is proposed for concrete footing/foundation work.

projects.name: 748 SAN BRUNO AVE
projects.description: This project proposes a tantamount to demolition of an existing single family dwelling and proposes a four story building (measuring approximately 4,250 gsf) with two new dwelling units which consist of three bedrooms each, along with two off-street vehicle parking spaces and two bicycle parking spaces. Each unit is provided with code-compliant usable open space in the form of decks and balconies.

projects.name: 1660 SHAFTER AVE
projects.description: Demolition of a one-story, single-family residence and construction of a new three-story, two-unit, residential building.

projects.name: 2045 SUTTER ST_1950 POST ST
projects.description: 100% affordable housing project. Addition of 5th story and new elevators in both existing 4-story buildings; 2045 Sutter Street (Building A - 16 new units) and 1950 Post St (Building B - 12 new units). Application 202110140447 and 202109098099 plans shared. Two applications on set of plans.

projects.name: 1939 Market
projects.description: The project site is located at the intersection of Market Street and Duboce Avenue and consists of two parcels that will be merged (APN 3501-006 & APN 3501-007). The proposed project consists of a 15-story high-rise residential building, with a total of 187 affordable apartments for seniors (a mix of studio, 1-Bedroom and 2-Bedroom units), residential interior amenity spaces and outdoor spaces. The building includes a ground floor commercial space, which will be provided in a "warm-shell" condition for a future tenant. The project includes on-site bike parking, and no on-site vehicle parking. The project will serve extremely low-income and low-income seniors with a portion of units reserved for seniors that have experienced homelessness; income restrictions will range from 15-60% MOHCD AMI.

projects.name: 50 8TH STREET
projects.description: The project proposal (“Project”) is to legalize the unauthorized conversion of 66 tourist Hotel rooms on the eighth and ninth floors of the BEI Hotel to 66 residential Group Housing units. The Project is eligible for administrative review as a 100% Affordable Housing Project under Planning Code Section 315 because all of the proposed Group Housing units would be restricted as affordable to households earning 120% or less of the Area Median Income (“AMI”). However, because the Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development (“MOHCD”) has not yet represented to the Planning Department that the Project is exempt from the Inclusionary Affordable Housing Program (Planning Code Section 415), the Project will provide additional on-site Below Market Rate (“BMR”) units at the following rates and levels of affordability: 10% of the 66 Project units at Very Low (50%) AMI; 2.5% at Low (80%) AMI; 2.5% at Middle (110%) AMI; and the remaining 85% at Moderate (120%) AMI. The Project seeks one development concession or incentive from the Planning Code’s requirement for residential usable open space (Section 135) under the State Density Bonus Law (CA Government Code Section 65915 et seq.), for which it is eligible through its provision of Very Low Income (50% of AMI) on-site BMR units; and with which it will comply as a “Shared Housing Building,” as that term is defined in CA Government Code Section 65915(o)(7)(A) and (B), through provision of one shared kitchen and a private microwave and refrigerator for each unit. By virtue of its status as a 100% Affordable Housing Project under Planning Code Section 315, the Project is eligible for administrative review and is exempt from the definitional requirement to provide one-half of one square-foot of interior common space for every square-foot of private residential space for the proposed Group Housing units.

projects.name: 160 Freelon (Land Dedication Site)
projects.description: This 100% affordable housing project will provide approximately 85 new residential units with associated common spaces, to be constructed on a 12,800-square-foot (0.3 acre) parcel, currently used as a private parking lot. Current adjacent uses are vacant parking lots and a vacant building to be developed into the 598 Brannan development consisting of three mixed-use buildings up to 185 feet tall comprising residential use, office, retail, PDR, and a public park. Project is supported and partially funded by the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development, the Low Income Housing Tax Credit program, and other funding sources. Project will serve extremely low- and low-income households. 25% of units will be set aside for permanent supportive housing making the project eligible for AB 2162. Proposed unit mix is approximately 18% studios, 28% one-bedrooms, 27% two-bedrooms, and 27% three-bedrooms. A 1:1 Class I bike storage ratio and no on-site car parking is proposed. Project is seeking approval under AB 2162 with State Density Bonus utilizing the following: Concessions: Living roof - Sec 249.78(d)(4) Active frontages - Sec 145.1 Waivers: Height - Sec 260 Narrow street setback - Sec 261.1 Lot coverage - Sec 249.78(d)(6)(A) Apparent mass reduction - Sec 261.1, 270 Horizontal mass reduction - Sec 270.1 Loading dimensions - Sec 152.1

projects.name: 850 Turk St MOHCD Project
projects.description: Tracking record for BPA 202212087884, "PRIORITY PROCESSING - 100% AFFORDABLE HOUSING. TO ERECT A 8-STORY, 92-DWELLING UNITS, TYPE 1A MIXED-USED BUILDING."

projects.name: 750 Golden Gate Phase 1
projects.description: 750 Golden Gate Ave Phase 1: 75 units, 100% affordable, on state land- permit 202401083599 T. Yanga 11/28/23: 750 GG is a State-owned parcel to be developed in 2 phases with 171 total units. Phase 1 is 75 units with 28 studios, 7 one-bedrooms, 19 two-bedrooms and 21 three-bedrooms. 45 of the 75 units will serve 36-107% AMI with 30 units will serve 140% AMI and will target teachers.

projects.name: 1500-1540 MARKET ST (aka 'One Oak') - Modified Project
projects.description: The Project Sponsor proposes modifications to the 1500-1540 Market Street (aka “One Oak”) residential development project, first approved by the Planning Commission on June 15, 2017. As modified, the proposed project (“Project”) would demolish two existing non-residential buildings and a surface parking lot and construct a new, approximately 508,000-square-foot residential building with a tower over podium design containing 541 dwelling units. The podium portion of the building is 14 stories high, with a roof height of approximately 139 feet, while the tower extends to 41 stories, reaching a roof height of 400 feet (or approximately 416 feet inclusive of mechanical equipment, and 436 feet tall inclusive of elevator overrun and rooftop screening). Three underground floor levels accommodate area for accessory off-street parking spaces, Class 1 bicycle parking, and MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) equipment. The ground floor will contain a community room and leasing office, residential lobby, building support and tenant service spaces, as well as vehicular access, parking, and loading spaces. The upper building levels will house dwelling units and recreational amenity areas. In total, the Project includes 135 off-street accessory parking spaces, three car share spaces, one off-street freight loading space, two off-street service loading vehicle spaces, as well as 210 Class 1 and 27 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. To further activate the ground floor experience, the Project would construct a public plaza and shared public right-of-way within a portion of the Oak Street (Oak Plaza). In addition, the existing on-site Muni elevator will remain in its current location, and a new weather protective enclosure will be constructed around it. The Project would necessitate approval of Planning Code Zoning Map amendment to reclassify the whole of the Project Site to the 140/400//140-450-R-4 Height and Bulk District, thereby increasing the base podium height from 120 feet to 140 feet and defining a base tower height of 400 feet on the western portion of the Project Site (Assessor’s Parcel 0836/005).

projects.name: 967 Mission (Land Dedication Site)
projects.description: The proposal is for a new 9-story residential building that would provide 94 units of rental housing for households earning less than 50% AMI with 25% of the units set aside for formerly homeless seniors, plus one manager’s unit, for a total of 95 units (63 studios and 32 one-bedrooms) with common laundry facilities, associated community space and supportive services, a roof deck, and no parking spaces. The project includes the demolition of a surface parking lot.

projects.name: 580 MINNA ST
projects.description: Proposed new construction of 7-story over basement residential building with 20 units (State Density Bonus Program).

projects.name: 98 Pennsylvania
projects.description: This proposal is a modification of the project that was approved by the Planning Commission on September 22, 2016 under Case No. 2013.0517ENX. The new project will utilize the State Density Bonus Program to construct a six-story, 70-foot-tall, 73,830-gross-square-foot residential building with 64 dwelling units.

projects.name: 249 Pennsylvania Family
projects.description: The proposed project is to construct a 9-story, 124-unit affordable, large family, housing building. At least 25% of the units will be 2-BR and 3BR each. At least 30% of the units will be 30%-AMI and permanently supportive. The remaining units, excluding the manager's unit, will be 50% AMI. The site is steeply sloped at approximately 10% along Pennsylvania Avenue. The main residential entry is at the first story near the street intersection. Residential services and amenities, including community room, property, manager and social services offices, bike parking, building utilities and storage are located on the first story. The second story includes residential units as well as the laundry room, ancillary community room, and an exit from the stories above. The third story includes residential units, a family day care unit, and the electrical room. The fourth through ninth story are similar and primarily contain residential units. The roof contains building utilities within an enclosed mechanical penthouse or visual / acoustical enclosure, a vegetated roof to mitigate stormwater, and photovoltaic panels. The roof will not be occupied except by for maintenance. Open space is located in a courtyard facing Pennsylvania Avenue on the on grade on the first story and over structure on the second story. Additional open space for stormwater treatment and for the family day care is located at level 3 at the south end of the site. The site is currently vacant with no existing uses or structures. The site is partially excavated and retained and contains existing retaining walls, shoring, slabs on grade, and perimeter fencing.

projects.name: 1196 Columbus
projects.description: The Project proposes the demolition of an existing one-story commercial building constructed in 1995 and the construction of a new 28,865 gsf, six-story, 60' high, building with 56 group housing rooms ("Project"). The Project will include 56 Class I and 4 Class 2 bicycle spaces and approximately 1,413 sq. ft. of usable open space. No off-street parking spaces are proposed. The Project will utilize the Individually-Requested State Density Bonus program (SDB). With the SDB, the project will request a reduction of the rear yard from the required 25% to 20%.

projects.name: 550 OFARRELL ST
projects.description: Demolish existing parking garage; construct 20-story residential building (212 feet in height) containing 158 dwelling units, including 19 affordable inclusionary units, 81 parking spaces. Utilizing the State Density Bonus law and Planning Code section 206.6, the project seeks a 50% density bonus over the 94 unit base project, with waivers for height, bulk, rear yard, and open space.

projects.name: 530-540 Turk St
projects.description: The proposed project would construct a 115-foot-tall, 11-story building that includes 100 dwelling units and ground floor retail. The Project would utilize the Individually Requested State Density Bonus program to increase residential density, with requests for waivers or concessions/incentives from development standards including rear yard (Section 134), usable open space (Section 135), dwelling unit exposure (Section 140), height (Section 250), and bulk (Section 270).

projects.name: 67-69 Belcher St
projects.description: The Project includes demolition of the existing two-story building, and new construction of a five-story, 56-ft tall, residential building (approximately 57,100 square feet (sq. ft.) total) with 31 dwelling units, 15 unbundled below-grade off-street parking spaces, 40 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces, and 2 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. The Project contains a dwelling-unit mix consisting of 11 three-bedroom units, 19 two-bedroom units, and 1 one-bedroom unit. The Project includes 3,879 square feet of common open space via ground floor rear yard and roof deck, and private open space for two units.

projects.name: 173 SHIPLEY ST
projects.description: The proposal is to erect a new 13-unit, seven-story building on a vacant lot utilizing the California State Density Bonus. The project will provide up to seven parking spaces, including one accessible van parking space, and 14 bicycle parking spaces (13 Class I and one Class II). The requested waivers are private open space, height limit, rear yard, and sun access plane. The requested incentives and concessions include parking maximum limits and bay window projection per Planning Code Section 136. The project would require approximately 35 cubic yards of excavation.

projects.name: 3275-3333 SAN BRUNO AVENUE
projects.description: The proposed project site is located east of San Bruno Avenue, west of the Bayshore Freeway, north of the intersection of Ordway Street and San Bruno Avenue, and south of the intersection of Mansell Street and San Bruno Avenue, and is composed of six parcels (block 5478, lots 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008). The project site is approximately 25,180 square feet (approximately 0.58 acres) in area. The site contains a billboard and is adjacent to a bus stop, but is otherwise vacant. The proposed project would merge the six lots into one and construct three new residential buildings with a total of 45 dwelling units, consisting of a 10-unit, three-story, approximately 10,090 gross square feet (gsf), approximately 29-foot-tall building at 3255 San Bruno Avenue; a 17-unit, three-story, approximately 14,890 gsf, approximately 33-foot-tall building at 3303 San Bruno Avenue; and an 18 unit, three-story, approximately 17,370 gsf, approximately 34-foot-tall building at 3333 San Bruno Avenue. Two of the buildings would include garage-level car parking spaces as follows: three spaces in 3255 San Bruno Avenue and 11 spaces in 3333 San Bruno. South of 3255 San Bruno, and the existing billboard, the project would include the construction of a proposed open space totaling approximately 8,950 square feet in area zoned as P(Public), which consists of easements for PG&E and SF Water. The existing billboard is located adjacent to the proposed 3255 San Bruno Avenue building and easements are located on portions of all six project site parcels. The easements take up approximately 8,220 square feet, or about 33 percent of the project area. A second open space totaling approximately 1,700 square feet in area would be added south of 3303 San Bruno Avenue and north of 3333 San Bruno Avenue, over the existing PG&E easement. The project would be supported by spread footing foundations and require 400 cubic yards of excavation for 3255 San Bruno Avenue, 380 cubic yards of excavation for 3303 San Bruno Avenue, and 420 cubic yards of excavation for 3333 San Bruno Avenue, for a total of 1,200 cubic yards of excavation. Construction is anticipated to take approximately 62 months. The project would need to relocate the existing bus stop approximately 5 feet south to accommodate the proposed curb cut for 3255 San Bruno. The project would be required to obtain a Street Improvement Permit from Public Works, and would need to coordinate with the bus stop advertiser for removal and installation of the existing bus shelter. The proposed project is seeking a density bonus, as well as waivers from planning code requirements related to rear yard, usable open space, large site citywide design standards, and ground floor residential; and concessions related to curb cuts, affordable housing tiers, and citywide design standards related to residential lobby entries.

projects.name: 134-150 PORTER STREET
projects.description: The proposed project will merge five vacant RH-2 zoned properties and develop the site as a single multifamily building. Using the State Density Bonus, the 10 allowable dwellings are proposed with a 100% bonus to equal 20 units. The total height will be seven stories tall but only three stories will be at street level.

projects.name: 1151 WASHINGTON ST
projects.description: The project site is a 3,571-square-foot parcel in the Nob Hill neighborhood. The project site is occupied by an existing 30-foot-tall, three-story, single-family residence that is approximately 3,050 square feet in size with two off-street parking spaces. Immediately east of the project site is a lower playground area of the Betty Ann Ong Recreation Center that is approximately 6 to 20 feet lower than the subject property’s rear yard. The change in elevation is supported by a retaining wall ranging between 6 to 20 feet that extends the length of the playground. Utilizing the state density bonus program, the project sponsor proposes the demolition of the existing single-family residence and construction of a 40-foot-tall (50-foot-tall with penthouses), four-story over basement residential building containing 10 for-sale townhouses and one off-street van parking space. The proposed building would be approximately 12,312 square feet in size. Each of the 10 residential units would be 4 stories and would include a penthouse and roof deck. The proposed front unit along Washington Street would be approximately 2,070 square feet in size with three bedrooms while the nine rear units would be approximately 940 square feet with two bedrooms. The proposed roof decks would include approximately 7-foot-tall privacy walls and there would be a mini-split heat pump (condenser unit) on the roof of each unit. Access to the proposed units would be from a 5-foot-wide pathway that would step up along the eastern edge of the property. The proposed pathway would include a bicycle ramp. Each unit would be equipped with an exterior hoist to facilitate the moving of furniture and other bulky items from the outside. The project would include 10 class 1 bicycle parking spaces and there would be 1 class 2 bicycle parking space on the sidewalk in front of project site. The existing 13-foot-wide curb cut would be reduced to a 10-foot-wide curb cut. The 6 existing trees on the subject property would be removed and the project would plant two trees in front of the project site. Trash and recycling for the proposed building would be located in the shared garage space located at the street level basement. The proposed development would be supported on micropiles. The project would require approximately 130 cubic yards of excavation with a depth of approximately 12.5 feet below ground surface. Construction duration is approximately 15 months.

projects.name: 2083 ELLIS ST
projects.description: The Project proposes construction of a new seven-story-over-basement building with nine new ownership units (eight net new) and demolition of a dilapidated, single-family residence (“SFR”). The SFR has been vacant since at least 2021, likely longer, and was owner-occupied from 1958 until it was vacated. The Project will provide one two-bedroom unit affordable to moderate-income households per the State Density Bonus Law.

projects.name: 641-645 48TH AVE
projects.description: The project proposes demolition of two existing single-family homes and the construction of nine new buildings containing a total of 20 residential units. The new development will be four stories and will include units of various sizes (studio, 2-bedroom, 3-bedroom, and 4-bedroom). Two units will be designated as affordable at 80% AMI.

projects.name: 3832 18th St
projects.description: The project sponsor proposes the demolition of the approximately 25-foot-tall, two-story, single-family residence and construction of a 60-foot-tall (68-foot-tall with elevator penthouse), six-story, residential building containing 19 group housing units. The proposed building would be approximately 11,147 gross square feet in size and would provide 890 square feet of common open space at the ground floor and 314 square feet of private open space at the 6th floor. The project would not provide off-street vehicular parking. The project proposes to use the state density bonus program.

projects.name: 222 CAPP ST
projects.description: Per SB 423, the proposal is to replace an existing surface parking lot with an eight-story, 70-unit project featuring residential uses above a podium with a lobby, utilities, and a private parking garage with 12 parking stalls. The project’s unit mix includes 21 studios, 21 one-bedrooms, and 28 two-bedrooms and its tenure is rental. A 2,000-square-foot, rear courtyard is featured on the second floor.

projects.name: 1010V Mission
projects.description: The proposed project (“Project”) is utilizing the Individually Requested State Density Bonus Program to achieve a roughly 8% density bonus and includes four waivers from: Rear Yard (Section 134), Exposure (Section 140), Bulk (Sec. 270) and Wind comfort criteria in exceedance (Sec. 148). The Project includes construction of an nine-story, 85-foot tall, 30,000 square foot, residential building with approximately 408 square foot community space fronting Mission Street and residential uses on floors 2-9 . The Project includes 57 housing units. The Project would provide 57 Class 1 and 4 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces.

projects.name: 1474 SOUTH VAN NESS AVE
projects.description: The proposed project employs SB423 for streamline approval process and the California State Density Bonus Law to: 1. Move, restore, and reuse historic front portion of existing single-family home to conform with allowable current zoning (matching the shortest setback of the adjoining neighbor front setback); 2. Vertical and horizontal addition up to 2-stories, including sculpting and setting back the new volume to conserve integrity of historical portion of building along South Van Ness; and 3. Vertical and horizontal addition to the building in the rear yard with 6 story new structure. A waiver is requested for the narrow street setback along Cypress Street and for an additional 10' of height on Cypress St. A total of 7 new dwelling units is proposed in addition to the 2 currently existing dwelling units, providing a total of 9 dwelling units on the property.

projects.name: 1728 Larkin Street
projects.description: The project site at 1728 Larkin Street, Assessor’s block and lot 0186/049, consists of a 3,491-square-foot rectangular lot currently improved with a one-story garage structure that was constructed in 1905 in the Nob Hill neighborhood. The extant garage is not a historic resource or a contributor to a historic resource district (Preservation Team Review Form, 1720-1724 Larkin Street, 9/28/2018). The project proposes to demolish the existing single-story garage structure and construct a 13,195-gross-square-foot (gsf), six-story, approximately 61-foot-tall (68’-11” tall to top of elevator penthouse) residential building with six dwelling units. The proposed six dwelling units would consist of one 1-bedroom unit, three 2-bedroom units, and two 3-bedroom units. The project would include an approximately 1,417 gsf garage on the basement and ground levels for six off-street parking spaces including one accessible space. The proposed garage would utilize a four-car parking stacker and be accessed from a 9-foot-wide curb cut on Larkin Street. Six class 1 bicycle parking spaces and two new electric vehicle charging stations would also be located on the ground floor. One new street tree would be installed along the frontage on Larkin Street. The project contains approximately 2,030 square feet of open space via private decks and a common roof deck. The project proposes to excavate approximately 865 cubic yards and install a reinforced mat concrete foundation with helical piers. Modified Project Description (9/17/2024): The modified project includes an increase in excavation, additional backyard retaining walls, and additional shoring. The proposed basement space has increased from 1,354 gross square feet to approximately 2,457 gross square feet.

projects.name: 224-228 CLARA ST
projects.description: The proposal is for a Conditional Use Authorization, pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303 and 317 to demolish a single-family residential building at 228 Clara Street and construct a five-story nine unit residential building on 224 and 228 Clara Streets.

projects.name: 400 BAY ST
projects.description: TO DEMOLISH 1 STORY RESTAURANT BUILDING. ** MAHER: N/A

projects.name: 815 - 821 Greenwich Street
projects.description: Vertical addition and interior remodel to the existing units. This project / permit is separate from the ADU legalization / addition.

projects.name: 888-898 UNION STREET
projects.description: Per the Housing Choice - San Francisco program, the proposal is to demolish the existing one-story parking garage structure and develop the lot with a four-story building consisting of two residential condominium housing units.

projects.name: 42 - 50 ALLEN ST
projects.description: Conversion of existing unconditioned garage and storage spaces into 2 ADU units and a utility room, in the existing 3-level multi-family building. Exterior scope of work is limited to demolition of the existing storage rooms in the rear yard and new windows. A voluntary seismic upgrade.

projects.name: 1074 UNION ST
projects.description: 1/10/24: The revised project includes three (3) Local program ADUs within existing ground floor parking garage and first floor below grade crawl space per Ordinance 162-16.

projects.name: 433-443 Lombard Street
projects.description: The project proposes to convert an existing unit (# 8) to a State mandated ADU.

projects.name: 642 LOMBARD ST
projects.description: The project proposes to add two new Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU), utilizing the Local ADU program per Planning Code Section 207.1, within an existing residential structure at the rear yard of the subject property. Exterior work includes a new egress stair and landing at the center of the lot, and replacement of the front gate. Response to complaint Nos. 202422936 and 201902761. Applicant to pay fee in lieu of two required street trees on a frontage of 30'-6".

projects.name: 2150 TAYLOR STREET
projects.description: Revision to 201907155920 to reconfigure unit 1 to make space for the existing meters, to consolidate units 2 and 3 into a single unit, to reconfigure the bike, mechanical, and laundry area, and to reconfigure the rear unit.

projects.name: 1918 POWELL ST
projects.description: The project proposes to alter the existing one-story garage with a vertical and horizontal addition to construct a 3-story over basement two-family residence with off-street parking. The project will also seek to legalize legal nonconforming structure in rear through DBI unit verification process. The proposed residential elevator would have a pit of 4 feet. Demolition and reconstruction for the existing garage structure is not approved without Mandatory Discretionary Review.

projects.name: 355 Lombard Street
projects.description: The project involves a three-story vertical addition to an existing one-story garage to create a new two-unit residential building. The project would require approximately 320 cubic yards of excavation.

projects.name: 31 HOUSTON ST
projects.description: Add two ADUs per Ord. 162-16 and update interior layout of existing ground floor unit. Exterior changes include infilling garage door on front facade; area to be infilled with stucco, with new aluminum-clad wood, double hung window and wood door installed in the infill area. Existing pedestrian entry door to be closed and relocated. Four additional aluminum-clad wood, double hung windows and one aluminum-clad casement window to be installed. Proposed project includes -Enclose three spaces under existing rear stairs for new bathrooms -Excavate partial first floor at West side for required dwelling unit ceiling height. Approx. 2' deep, 49 cubic yd -Construct new retaining wall in order to reinforce West side of the property.

projects.name: 572 CHESTNUT ST - Modified Project
projects.description: Install (2) New Accessory Dwelling Units at the basement level, pursuant to Planning Code Section 207.1. CEQA determination can be found under Planning Record No. 2025-001970PRJ.

projects.name: 740 WASHINGTON ST

The proposed project would demolish the existing building and construct an approximately 65-foot-tall, six-story-over-basement, 47,329-square-foot residential building with 25 dwelling units (12 one-bedroom units, 9 two-bedroom units, and four three-bedroom units). A new 10-foot-wide curb cut on Washington Street would provide access to the new garage, replacing the existing 64-foot-wide curb cut. A main entrance along Washington Street would provide pedestrian access to the building lobby. Two bicycle parking spaces and four new street trees would be installed in the public right of way along the Washington Street frontage. The project would include 6,078 square feet of open space for building residents in a combination of private roof terraces and rear yards, and a common roof deck. The new building would be supported by a mat or spread footing foundation. projects.description: Pursuant to Planning Code Section 317(c)(7)(A), the project proposes the removal of a vacant, unauthorized dwelling unit created within an existing non-residential building. The unauthorized unit does not comply with open space or dwelling unit exposure requirements and is ineligible to be legalized pursuant to Section 307, Section 207(c)(4), Section 207(c)(6), or Section 207.3 and is, therefore, exempt from the Conditional Use Authorization requirement. The unauthorized unit was installed within the existing commercial space without a permit and used only by family members of the owner; it was never rented or otherwise occupied by a tenant. As depicted in the plans and diagrams, the unauthorized unit does not comply with applicable open space or dwelling unit exposure requirements of the MUR Zoning District (Showplace Square / Potrero Hill Plan Area). Specifically, the unauthorized unit opens onto a non-residential surface parking lot and approximately 5-foot-wide shared alleyways used for access and egress by neighboring commercial tenants located in other spaces within the property. The project proposes limited interior building demolition; no exterior modifications to the existing commercial building are proposed.

projects.description: The 4,700 square foot project site is located on a down-sloping lot on the east side of Jamestown Avenue east of Griffith Street, with frontage on Jamestown Avenue and on the pedestrian trail portion of Gilroy Street. The proposed project would subdivide the existing vacant lot into three substandard-sized lots, each fronting on Jamestown Avenue. The northernmost Lot A at 778 Jamestown Avenue would be approximately 1,502 square feet, Lot B at 768 Jamestown Avenue would be approximately 1,585 square feet, and Lot C at 758 Jamestown Avenue would be approximately 1,596 square feet. The project would construct a four-story, 34-foot tall, three-bedroom, single family dwelling on each lot. Each dwelling unit would have two vehicle parking spaces in an individual, street-level garage accessed by a 10-foot-wide curb cut on Jamestown Avenue and a rear yard. The proposed buildings on Lots B and C would have second-floor rear decks. The project is seeking variances from the Planning Code for three substandard-sized lots and to address front setbacks. Details regarding the lot dimensions and front setbacks are shown on project plans dated December 13, 2018. During the approximately 18-month construction period, excavation of approximately 600 cubic yards of material would occur to a maximum depth of approximately 12 feet. Foundation Recommendations Pursuant to the geotechnical investigation prepared for the project (Frank Lee & Associates. February 6, 2018. Soil and Foundation Investigation Proposed Three Four-Story Residential Building 758, 768, 778 Jamestown Avenue, San Francisco, California 94124), the proposed buildings should be supported by drilled piers with grade beams constructed between the piers. The piers should extend 10 – 15 feet into competent soils or bedrock which was encountered at approximately 13.5 feet. An alternate foundation system that could be used would be a concrete mat slab with a perimeter continuous footing to control moisture migration as described in the geotechnical report.

The 18,740 square-foot site is vacant except for a double-sided billboard that would be removed as part of the proposed project. The proposed project would merge the six lots into one and construct a 65-foot tall, 69,460-square-foot building with 66,130 square feet of residential space and 5,805 square feet of common usable open space, consisting of a 2,090-square-foot rear yard and a 3,715-square-foot roof deck. Additionally, 88 of the proposed dwelling units would have private balconies that would provide usable open space. The project would include 100 dwelling units comprised of 17 studios, 37 one-bedroom, 21 two-bedroom, and 25 three-bedroom units. Of these units, 30 units would be offered at below market rates under the HOME-SF program. The proposed project would not include a backup diesel generator and would not include off-street vehicular parking. Two new street trees and landscaping would be planted along 3rd Street. Primary pedestrian access to the residential lobby would be provided on 3rd Street. Consistent with city bicycle parking requirements, the proposed project would provide 100 class I bicycle parking spaces within the building and six class II bicycle parking spaces along the project frontage on 3rd Street. One existing curb cut immediately adjacent to the northernmost crosswalk would be removed and filled in as part of the project. The sidewalk along 3rd Street would also be expanded to 10 feet along the project frontage. Construction of the project would disturb approximately 18,700 square feet of soil and require excavation to a maximum depth of 31 feet below ground surface for construction of the building’s mat slab foundation. The project would excavate approximately 12,000 cubic yards of soil. Project construction is anticipated to last 22 months. No pile driving is proposed.

The project proposes to merge the existing two lots into one lot. The project would also remodel the existing home, add an accessory dwelling unit, an estimated 220-sf deck, landscaping, two Class 1 bicycle parking spaces and remove an existing extension to a wooden shed. The project also proposes to construct two new two-unit buildings, located closer to the Fountain Street frontage. The proposed building located at 22-24 Fountain Street would be approximately 5,600 sf in size and include three floors of living space over a basement level plus decks on the third floor and the roof. The second proposed building at 26-28 Fountain Street would be approximately 6,000 sf in size and similar in design to the 22-24 Fountain Street proposed building. Open space for the new buildings would be provided through a combination of rear yards and private third floor and roof decks. Each new building would include two on-site vehicular parking spaces and two Class 1 bicycle spaces at the basement level. Two new curb cuts, approximately 10 feet wide, are proposed on Fountain Street for access to each new building’s garage space. The project would add two new street trees along the Fountain Street frontage. The project requires excavation to approximately 33 feet below grade for a proposed elevator pit and removal of 2,300 cubic yards of material for the installation of a combination mat slab and buttressed retaining wall foundation. Construction is anticipated to last approximately 16 months.

The proposed dwelling unit mix consists of, 17 one-bedroom units, 11 two-bedroom units, and one three-bedroom unit. Of these 29 units, six of the units would be inclusionary affordable units. The project would apply the provisions of HOME-SF Guidelines. No backup diesel generator would be located on-site. With regards to common open space, the project would provide 1,489 square feet of common open space on the third floor and 2,644 square feet of common open space on the rooftop deck; in total, the project includes 4,133 square feet of common open space. In addition, seven new street trees would be planted on the project’s frontage along Mission Street and Florentine Avenue. Primary pedestrian access to the residential lobby would be provided on Florentine Avenue. Vehicles would access the basement parking garage via the proposed vehicle ramp and new 10-foot curb-cut on Florentine Avenue. Consistent with city bicycle parking requirements, the proposed project includes 37 secured class I bicycle parking spaces and six class II bicycle parking spaces on the project’s Mission Street and Florentine Avenue frontages. The existing 12-foot sidewalk on Mission Street and 8-foot sidewalk on Florentine Avenue would be replaced with new sidewalks per DPW requirements. Two existing curb cuts on Mission St would be removed and a new 10-foot curb cut on Florentine Avenue would be constructed to provide garage access. The proposed project also includes a new 30-foot commercial loading zone on Mission Street near the Florentine Avenue intersection. Construction of the project would disturb approximately 2,600 square feet of soil and require excavation to a maximum depth of 6 feet below ground surface for construction of the building’s basement level and spread footing foundation. The project would excavate approximately 1,000 cubic yards of soil. Project construction is anticipated to last 18 to 24 months. No pile driving is proposed.

projects.name: 835 Turk
projects.description: The property at 835 Turk Street is a seven-story-over-basement, residential hotel built in 1928. The building occupies the length of the property with the ground floor accessed from Turk Street and the basement floor accessed from the back of the building at Elm Street. Built per 1928 SF Building Law Class C, the building has an open main stair, an additional staircase at the Elm Street side, and a fire escape at the Turk Street façade. Two elevators service the lobby and the floors above. The building contains parking (not striped for ADA parking and clear height less than required for ADA), storage, and mechanical rooms at the basement floor. The lobby level (ground floor) consists of a property maintenance office, parking (not striped for ADA parking and clear height less than required for ADA), a maintenance office, and a laundry room. The floors above include regular units, a one-bedroom manager's unit, and a kitchen/dining/lounge area at the first upper floor. The regular units contain bathrooms but no kitchens. The manager's unit contains a bathroom and a kitchen. The construction is concrete with supporting steel structure, wood floor construction at the upper floors, and wood roof construction. The basement floor is not in the project scope except as required for improvements to the building. The parking will remain not striped for ADA parking and clear height to remain less than required for ADA parking. The required scope at the basement includes structural brace frames, improvements to the Elm Street side stairs, and removing or abandoning MEP equipment and piping. The ground floor use as a parking garage will be changed to become support spaces for the residential use of the building. At the first upper floor, the one-bedroom manager’s unit and the kitchen/dining/lounge area will be converted to become ADA-compliant. At all residential floors, two units at each floor will be combined into one mobility unit and the remaining space will be used to add a trash room with a new chute. The existing R2 SRO building with 114 units, including unit #101 currently used as common space, will be reduced to 108 units to provide required mobility units. Unit #101 will continue to be used as common space. Windows will be replaced as needed.
